chapters.title: Chapter 4380 The Civilization of Mana! I
paragraphs: "My people."
His voice wasn't loud, but it was heavy!
Every being heard him as if he stood beside them personally.
"My Civilization."
He let the words settle, felt the way they resonated through the collective existence of everyone present.

"You have lived. You have waited. You have formed the backbone of our Civilization through perseverance that spans many years. Through isolation that would have broken lesser peoples. Through challenges I can only begin to imagine."
His gaze swept across them all.
"And now... it is time to let it bloom."
The surrounding Mana pulsed in response to his words.

"Your Civilization shall be isolated no more. At this moment, at this instant, I declare that our Civilization can finally bloom! The barriers that kept you contained are lifted. The restrictions that prevented your expansion are removed. What you have built in isolation will now spread across external existence, and the powers that thought themselves eternal will learn what it means to face a Civilization that refined itself through desperation and...Mana."
He paused, and looked at all those here.
"You have exceeded every expectation. You have justified the faith I placed in you when I established this isolated pocket. And now, together, we will show existence itself what Mana truly means."
His body glimmered blue.
HUUUM!
And then his Infinite Mana...the foundational element of his existence...erupted.
An endless sea of pure blue Mana gushed from his form, cascading outward like an ocean that had been dammed for too long and was finally released!
It bloomed across the sky, washing over every being present, flowing through the vast structures of this isolated Civilization, painting everything in his signature authority.
Kael trembled as the mana touched him, his voice breaking with emotion.
"Ah, truly... as we theorized, as we hoped... The Ancestor's mana is... Infinite!"
WAA!
The word echoed across the space with the weight of confirmed revelation.
BOOM!
Even Riya, floating beside Noah with her characteristic defiance, seemed to tremble slightly as his mana washed over her.
Her jewel-blue eyes widened fractionally, her rebellious expression faltering for just a moment as she felt the sheer endlessness of what he was offering!
Oh!
But she recovered quickly, her face settling back into its defiant glare as she harrumphed softly.
As his mana continued washing over the Civilization...over buildings and beings and the very fabric of this isolated realm, all those present responded with synchronized movement.
They straightened, every single being, their forms blazing with
authority as they took their right hands and placed their fists over their hearts.
Hearts filled with Mana. Hearts that beat with his Way. Hearts that recognized their Architect!
And as one, millions of voices bellowed!
"ANCESTOR!"
HUUM!
The word shook existence.
The surrounding space actually trembled, the collective authority of millions of powerful beings focused into a single declaration of loyalty
and recognition.
Existential Trembling from the call!
Noah looked at his people as they all gazed toward him, paying
respects.
This was acknowledgment of bond. Of connection deeper than words
could convey!
He smiled and raised one hand in a calming gesture.
"There is much to be done," he said, his voice booming with a quiet command. "Get things in order. Organize yourselves. Prepare for what
comes next."
He paused.
"Soon, those who wish to explore external existence will be given that choice. The barriers are lifted. The isolation ends. For those who have been waiting to see what lies beyond this pocket...
His smile widened slightly.
"Your patience will be rewarded."
At such words, Kael stepped forward immediately, his authority
exerting itself with practiced ease.
"You heard the Ancestor! Return to your duties! Organize your sectors! Prepare for the integration protocols we've been planning for centuries! Move with purpose!"
His commands carried the weight of someone who'd been leading this Civilization for many years, and the floating millions responded with disciplined efficiency.
They dispersed, flowing away like water finding its level, returning to
the various structures and towers and floating rings that made up
their home.
Within moments, only a small group remained floating near Noah and
Kael.
The surrounding space flickered...
And forty-six additional figures manifested.

The other Original Seed Members, each one blazing with 50 Quintillion in both Complexity and Purity. Forty-six beings who had been there at the beginning, who had received Noah's initial gift and then spent millions of years perfecting what he'd given them.
They bowed as one.
"Ancestor," they said in unison, "we welcome you home." One stepped forward, and he shared certain characteristics with Riya. His eyes were the same jewel-blue, though his carried more
discipline, more control.
"Ancestor" he said, bowing deeply. "I am the father to that troublesome Riya of mine. It is an honor beyond words to have you
here."
Another moved forward, a woman whose white-blue hair flowed like
liquid mana.
"I am Laaphina. I have spent 600,000 years refining techniques for
mana circulation across large populations. I am eager to demonstrate
what we've achieved."
They continued introducing themselves once more, each Original
Seed Member offering brief identification and expressions of
reverence.
Kael smile with happiness,
exasperation.
en waved them away with affectionate
"Don't suffocate the Ancestor! There will be time for detailed
presentations later! For now, let me show him what we've accomplished without overwhelming him..."
The Seed Members laughed and began dispersing, though they cast frequent glances back toward Noah as if confirming he was real and not some shared hallucination. Riya rolled her eyes dramatically.
"You're all being too ceremonial," she said,"Ancestor, you don't want to
see any of these old things, right? Let me show you one of the more
cool places I helped design. Something actually interesting instead of boring weavings"
Without waiting for input from Noah, from Kael, from anyone...Riya appeared beside Noah in a blur of movement.
Her hand landed on his shoulder...
And they disappeared.
WAP!
"RIYA!"
Kael's bellow of frustration echoed across the realm, his form blazing
with impotent anger at yet another instance of her complete disregard for protocol.
Voltrax appeared beside him.
"Brother Kael, she's taken him to that place. You know, the one she's
actually proud of. We should follow slowly."
He paused, then added with genuine observation.
"You remember how The Ancestor is. Easy-going, adaptable. He won't
punish Riya for enthusiasm, even if it's wrapped in disrespect. If anything, he probably appreciates the lack of ceremony."
Kael's expression hardened.
"Fine." he muttered.
Noah's vision cleared as the movement completed, and he found
himself standing in front of a massive structure shining glorious blue.
Riya floated beside him, her form blazing with barely contained excitement as she executed an exaggerated bow.
"O Great Ancestor," she said, sarcasm dripping from every word, "I welcome you to the Mana Glyph Genesis Grounds! A place for the
generation and storage of Mana Glyphs and Mana Arcana Glyphs that
I helped design!" She straightened, smiling broadly.
"Well... 'helped design' might be understating it. I basically built the
whole fucking thing with some assistance from Uncle Kael and a few others who knew theoretical framework better than me."
Noah's eyes pulsed, expanding his perception to drink in every detail
of what he was witnessing.
The structure was massive...hundreds of miles in diameter, shaped like a perfect three-dimensional representation of the Mana Glyph for Fireball.
The walls glowed with compressed Mana, each surface inscribed with

millions of smaller Glyphs that fed power into the central structure. Around the perimeter, a few dozen beings worked...Citizens of the Civilization who stopped their tasks to bow deeply toward Noah, their expressions showing awe and reverence that made the surrounding Mana ripple.
"You said the generation and storage of Glyphs?" he said slowly. Riya's expression transformed. She puffed her chest out, floating slightly higher as if her excitement was physically lifting her.

"Yes! This place was specifically designed to allow for the rapid elevation of those weaker than us by harnessing mana from more powerful beings and atmospheric mana to outwardly form Mana Glyphs and Mana Arcana Glyphs."

Her eyes blazed with tendrils of Mana. "The more fucking frustrating and intricate part that took me ages to figure out..." She gestured dramatically at various sections of the structure. "...was allowing them to stay active in nature without being bound to anyone initially, and then successfully having them ready for merging and fusion with any compatible recipient!"
She grabbed Noah's hand suddenly...this being with 61 Quintillion Complexity casually seizing his arm like someone excited and showing off their art project.
"Come on! Let me show you how it works!" Noah couldn't help but smile as he went forward.
His Isolated Civilization had exceeded expectations in ways he hadn't
even imagined to anticipate!
And there seemed to be much more in store!

chapters.title: Chapter 4381 The Civilization of Mana! II
paragraphs: They moved through wide blue halls that pulsed with concentrated Mana, the walls themselves alive with flowing power.
The architecture here was functional, every line and curve serving a purpose in the greater mechanism of Glyph generation.
As they walked, Riya talked, her words tumbling out with the enthusiasm.
"So the Old Things, Uncle Kael and the other Seed Members, they were stuck for ages trying to figure out how to make this work," she said, gesturing broadly at the surrounding structure.
"They understood the theory, could manipulate Mana Glyphs individually, but the systematic generation and storage part? That kept eluding them."
Her jewel-blue eyes blazed with satisfaction.

"Then I came along, and my sensitivity for Mana... fuck, it's hard to explain. I can feel the building blocks of every single Glyph. Not just perceive them...I mean feel them, like touching fabric and
understanding how every thread connects."
She stopped and breathed in the Mana in their surroundings before she turned to him with luminous eyes shining with a tinge of craziness to say...
"I. Fucking. Love. Mana."
He stared with fascination at this odd anomaly and eventually smiled. "Me too."
She shook her head as if he didn't understand and led him around a corner, the hallway opening into something vaster.

"Because of my love for Mana, everything was easy for me. The Mana Glyph of the Primordial Fireball, the one everybody starts with, that was the first one I completely broke down into individual components. As long as you know and understand the smallest possible building blocks of the Glyph, even if an existence isn't actively guiding the Mana, you can set up those building blocks to produce the same results."
Noah's perception sharpened, following her logic.
"You made the process...automated?" he asked.
"Yes!" Riya's expression lit up with the joy of being understood. "Automated Glyph formation through precise arrangement of fundamental Mana components. But then we hit another problem."
Her tone shifted, becoming more technical.

"After a Glyph is formed, it needs a host...an existence to occupy it. Otherwise, it dissipates after a period of time. The building blocks collapse in on themselves and disappear. The Glyph just... unmakes itself because it has no existential anchor."
She paused at a junction, then continued down a side passage.

"When we arrived at that point, the next step became obvious. We had to naturally form containers filled with Mana...but a unique type of Mana that could be distinguished as if it were an existence itself."
Noah's eyes flashed with understanding.
Riya continued.

"This turned out to be something fairly simple to do for those with extreme attunement to Mana like me. All you have to do is give Mana personality, basically trick the Glyphs into thinking the area they occupy is an Existence instead of empty space. Create pseudo-consciousness through precise mana manipulation." She gestured ahead as the hallway opened into something
magnificent.
"And these containers are... right here."
They emerged onto a bridge...vast, crystalline, and spanning across a chamber so large Noah's perception had to expand significantly to encompass its full scope.
All around them, extending in every direction across multiple levels connected by additional bridges, glass-like circular containers floated in organized arrays.
Thousands of them, perhaps tens of thousands, each one pulsing with blue light.
Each container bore labels...elegant script formed from compressed Mana that identified the specific Glyph type stored within.
And inside each container...
Noah's eyes widened slightly.
Thousands upon thousands of Mana Glyphs, floating in organized
patterns within their glass-like prisons, each one active, stable,
waiting to be claimed.
His gaze locked onto a massive container directly ahead...easily a hundred meters in diameter, its label reading "PRIMORDIAL FIREBALL" in letters that blazed with appropriate heat.
Inside that single container, thousands of the Mana Glyph of Primordial Fireball rotated in complex orbital patterns.
"These," Riya said, her voice carrying pride, "are what we call the Repositories of Formed Authority. Containers that hold countless Mana Glyphs within them, stable and ready for integration."

She leaned against the bridge's railing, her posture casual but her eyes serious as she watched Noah process what he was seeing. "With this achievement, any Citizen of our Civilization can be granted access to enter these chambers and begin fusing with as many Mana
Glyphs as they can handle. They don't have to spend years forging them individually, they just come here, connect with the Repository, and absorb pre-formed Glyphs that integrate immediately."
Her expression held weight beyond simple achievement.
"This is one of the main reasons why the average Complexity and

Purity of many existences in our Civilization is approximately above 8 Quintillion. We've systematized the advancement process to a degree that makes individual genius almost unnecessary. Anyone with sufficient dedication can reach heights that would be considered impossible in external existence."
Noah stood there, his perception drinking in the scope of what they'd
accomplished.
Automated Glyph generation. Stable storage without degradation. Mass distribution systems that allowed an entire Civilization to advance at rates that defied normal progression.
His other members of this Civilization in The Infiniverse...were going
to love this!
"You all have done..." He paused, searching for words adequate to the accomplishment. "...a lot."
The understatement buzzed.
Riya shifted her position, putting her back against the railing with her
hands laid coolly on the rail's surface. She looked at Noah with an expression that had lost its characteristic excitement, her gaze
turning serious as she studied him.
Noah continued staring at the many different
containers...Repositories for Fireball, for Mana Barrage, Mana Shield,
and other unique abilities. It felt like a huge library opening up its legs
to him!
Off to the side, Riya continued to stare at him silently. The silence stretched, comfortable but weighted.
Eventually, Noah spoke without turning to look at her.
"You seem to have something on your mind this whole time," he said
quietly. "What is it?"
At such words, in the serious mood that had settled over them both, Riya's expression hardened.
"You kept us locked in here for all these countless years," she said, her voice having none of its normal sarcasm.
"Told Uncle Kael to forge the Civilization to the highest possible heights he could because something catastrophic was coming in the
future."
Her jewel-blue eyes remained fixed on him.
"You kept us locked in here with the promise that eventually we'd be
called forth. But that same moment...the moment we'll finally be able to move out freely...we may be met with catastrophe immediately. How should we feel about that, O Glorious Ancestor?"
HUUM!
Noah turned to look at her, his tyrannical gaze steady and
unflinching.
"Catastrophe was always coming," he said, his voice holding the
weight of absolute certainty, "before I came across your uncles and your father."
He held her gaze.
"There was an Early Creature who was the catastrophe. Maybe if I

hadn't intervened at that time, that Early Creature would have violated those who wanted to violate, then extinguished everyone in your village...everyone who are now the Seed Members of this Civilization."
His tone didn't change, remaining calm and factual. "Maybe they wouldn't have killed everyone. Maybe you all would have
continued to live in shame and fear as who knows what would have happened. But catastrophe has always been there. It may have been even closer without my intervention."
He paused.
"And the only thing I did was try to provide a chance...a capability to

survive a distant catastrophe. Which gave your uncles, your aunts, your father, and you millions of years to enjoy in isolation. Meanwhile, me and other members of our Civilization of Mana who exist in a different time? We have not had that much time to spend."

At such words, Riya blinked, her serious expression breaking as something like understanding crossed her features. A smile tugged at her lips. "How...old are you, Ancestor?" she asked, genuine curiosity in her
voice.

"Catastrophe was always coming," he said, his voice holding the
weight of absolute certainty, "before I came across your uncles and your father."
He held her gaze.
"There was an Early Creature who was the catastrophe.
Maybe if I

hadn't intervened at that time, that Early Creature would have violated those who wanted to violate, then extinguished everyone in your village...everyone who are now the Seed Members of this Civilization."
His tone didn't change, remaining calm and factual.
"Maybe they wouldn't have killed everyone.
Maybe you all would have
continued to live in shame and fear as who knows what would have happened.
But catastrophe has always been there.
It may have been even closer without my intervention."
He paused.
"And the only thing I did was try to provide a chance...a capability to
survive a distant catastrophe.
Which gave your uncles, your aunts, your father, and you millions of years to enjoy in isolation.
Meanwhile, me and other members of our Civilization of Mana who exist in a different time?
We have not had that much time to spend."
At such words, Riya blinked, her serious expression breaking as something like understanding crossed her features.
A smile tugged at her lips.
"How...old are you, Ancestor?" she asked, genuine curiosity in her
voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 4382 The Civilization of Mana! III
paragraphs: The question made Noah pause, his expression showing slight trouble as if performing calculations.
He had existed in multiple time frames. Had moved to the Earliest Folds before returning to the current era, with eons passing between those transitions. But he hadn't lived those eons....

In totality, his actual age was still measured in dozens of years. Less than thirty, if he was being precise about subjective experience. He looked at this member of his Civilization...this being who was millions of years old from her perspective, who had lived through generations of development, and spoke simply.
"I can be considered less than a hundred years old."
Riya's mouth opened in shock, her eyes widening with genuine surprise.
Then she moved toward him, floating closer to examine him with renewed interest, actually sniffing his figure again as she processed this information.
"The Ancestor was actually a baby," she said, her voice holding wonder mixed with amusement. "Wow. Don't tell anyone else this, or they might lose all their respect for you, Little Ancestor."
Little Ancestor?
Noah shook his head at the audacity of the title, but amusement touched the edges of his expression.
He looked at this strongest member of his Civilization and asked calmly, "Were you and the Seed Members able to come up with any method of avoiding catastrophe, as I instructed?"
The atmosphere shifted instantly.
Riya's playful expression vanished.
She looked at Noah in silence, the weight of nearly years of preparation settling across her features.
Finally, she sighed.
"Maybe," she said quietly. "And maybe not, O Great Ancestor."
She turned away slightly, her gaze drifting toward the countless Repositories floating around them.

"You know, many of those here have been expectantly waiting for your call. We all believed that you would eventually come and call us out of isolation. Everyone was so fucking excited about it...Uncle Kael most of all. They've been preparing for this moment for millions of years."
Her voice took on a different quality.

"But while so many others were looking forward to this moment, I actually dreaded you appearing. Because it meant that even though the thing I wanted most would finally come...that our isolation would end and we'd be able to see existence in its fullest...your call to us would also mean that whatever catastrophe you've been preparing us for, whatever catastrophe this entire Civilization was built to fight off, is also near."
She turned back to face him directly, her jewel-blue eyes blazing with emotion.

"So I was dreading your arrival because it meant everything I love and hold dear also has a chance of ending soon after we're finally freed. Everyone I've known for millions of years. Every place I've helped build. All of it... potentially gone."
She moved closer, her expression intense as seas of heavy Mana pulsed around her.

"So I want to ask you, O Powerful Ancestor...you are now here at this glorious moment. Can you promise? Can you promise me that with everything this Civilization can give you, with all the power that you have with your Infinite Mana, that I will not lose all those I hold dear?"
Her voice burned with desperate weight.
"That with your lead, we will survive this coming catastrophe? Can you promise me that?"
She asked him for an extremely heavy promise.
Noah looked at this strongest member of his Civilization...this being who could probably solo entire Folds, but who stood before him now asking for assurance he couldn't guarantee.
His expression remained steady, his tyrannical gaze meeting her desperate one without flinching.
"I can only promise things that I am certain of," he said.
"And I do not yet have certainty when it comes to surviving The Fallout. When it comes to surviving THE Loom and whatever forces
they command."
He paused.

"But even though I do not have certainty, I will continue to do everything that I can to make sure that my Civilization...that my family, of which this Isolated Civilization is now a part, survives. I will continue to do everything that I can, give My Everythings, to ensure our survival in the coming Fallout."
Everything.
His Everythings!
Oh!

"I cannot promise victory. But I can promise that I will exhaust every possibility, violate every limitation, and defy every predetermined outcome to create a path forward. That is what I do. That is what I am. And I will not stop until either we have survived, or I have been completely unmade in the attempt."
HUUM!
Riya became silent.
Eventually, she gave a light nod.
Then she sighed, stretching her arms above her head as if physically
shaking off the heavy mood.
"Okay, Ancestor," she said, her characteristic irreverence returning.
"Let's fucking do this."
She waved her hands, and in front of them, an illusory diagram bloomed into existence.

It showed a complex circular structure made of interwoven mana patterns...layers upon layers of defensive architecture, Glyphs, Haki.... all integrated into a unified whole that made Noah's mind immediately
engage.
"I give you," Riya said, her voice holding pride and concern in equal measure, "the theoretical model to survive any catastrophe, built around our own Isolated Civilization as its core."
The diagram rotated, revealing additional complexity with each
revolution.
"The Bastion of Mana...the protective construct designed to house an

entire Civilization. We've been refining the theory for 400,000 years, running simulations, testing components in isolation. But the last ingredient to potentially bring it to full fruition, to test if it will
actually withstand a potential catastrophe...
She looked at Noah directly.
"You are that last ingredient, O Ancestor."
Noah's perception locked onto the diagram, drinking in every detail as
Riya continued.

"The Bastion of Mana, at its most theorized success, is a shelter powered by one hundred entities functioning as Nodes of Mana. Each Node must hold at the very minimum 1,000 Quintillion in both Complexity and Purity...enough power to maintain the defensive architecture even under catastrophic assault."
She gestured at specific points on the diagram where concentrated power signatures were marked.

"These hundred Nodes form the foundational structure, the pillars that hold everything together. But at its forefront, at the absolute center of the entire construct, there needs to be someone who holds boundless weavings of Mana. Someone whose reserves are functionally infinite, who can feed power into the system continuously without ever depleting."
Her gaze remained fixed on Noah.
"That someone would be you, Ancestor. Your Infinite Mana is the only
thing we've theorized could power the Bastion at full capacity indefinitely. Without that central pillar, the hundred Nodes would eventually exhaust themselves. With you at the center..."
She paused, hope entering her expression.
"With you at the center, the Bastion could theoretically withstand
anything. Existential collapse. Reality unmaking. Whatever form The Fallout takes. As long as the structure holds and you maintain the power flow, everyone inside would be protected."
Noah studied the diagram, his mind racing through calculations!
One hundred Nodes at minimum 1,000 Quintillion each. That was 100,000 Quintillion in aggregate defensive power, distributed across the structure!
And at the center, himself...providing the endless energy that would keep the entire system operational.
It was ambitious. It was audacious. It was glorious of a possibility!

"With the resources of external existence, with access to whatever advancement opportunities exist in the First Folds and beyond, we could probably elevate enough beings to the necessary threshold within... I don't know, depends on the timeline we're working with.
Years? Decades?"
Her expression turned questioning.
"How long do we have before we all die, Ancestor? Before The Fallout
arrives?"
Noah's expression became contemplative.
"Unknown," he said calmly. "Could be years. Could be months. Could
be days."
Riya stared forth blankly before she cursed.
"That fucking sucks ass."
He looked at the diagram again, his tyrannical mind already working

through it. "Haa. then let's get started, Little Ancestor," she said, smiling despite the weight of what they were discussing. "We've got a lot of fucking work to do, and apparently not much time to do it in..."

chapters.title: Chapter 4383 The Civilization of Mana! IV
paragraphs: Riya seemed enthusiastic to get started!
Noah stood before the illusory diagram of the Bastion of Mana, his perception drinking in every detail.
One hundred Nodes at minimum 1,000 Quintillion each.
The number alone was staggering because achieving it at scale presented challenges that even he would have to pause at.
Is it even possible to raise that many beings to 1,000 Quintillion before The Fallout arrives?
The thought circled through his consciousness.
He'd been climbing through the Quintillion ranges himself, and the experience had taught him brutal lessons about the limitations inherent in existential advancement.
There was the clear Ceiling that Ruination spoke of in detail!
Not a soft limit that could be pushed through sheer effort...a hard ceiling built into the fundamental weavings of Existence.

Devouring beings at 5 Quintillion Complexity and Purity would only ever get you toward that level. It didn't matter if you consumed one such being or a thousand...you'd approach 5 Quintillion, but never exceed it through that method alone.
This had been made clear.
Which meant traditional looting and devouring, while effective for early advancement, became increasingly inefficient past certain thresholds!
His own means were more effective.
The Cultivation Citadel of The Early Creature could grant harvests exceeding 5 Quintillion per day if used optimally.
The pressure-based advancement combined with his Principle of Perpetual Harvest created multiplicative effects that showed the glory of his way.
If I could get many in My Civilization to reach the 10 Quintillion threshold sufficient to withstand the Citadel's pressure, their power would begin rising rapidly.
The strategy formed itself naturally in his mind.

Bring all his Civilization members into the Citadel's crushing environment, let them grind under impossible weight while Perpetual Harvest amplified their gains, and watch them skyrocket toward the thresholds necessary for the Bastion's Nodes.
Of course, that assumed they had time!
That assumed The Fallout wouldn't arrive before sufficient numbers reached necessary power levels.
Too many unknowns. Too many variables he couldn't control yet.
He turned slightly, his analytical gaze shifting from the diagram to Riya, who stood nearby watching him with intensity.
Her jewel-blue eyes tracked across his form with focus as if she was studying him, or trying to see or confirm something that she was not being entirely clear about.
Their gazes met, and a slow smile spread across Riya's features.
"Are you checking me out, Ancestor?" she asked.
Before Noah could respond, another voice cut in from the distance.
"Why would the Ancestor want your scrawny ass, Riya?"
Behind them, Kael and several other Seed Members materialized as they had been close behind.
An older woman floated among them, her form blazing with 50 Quintillion Complexity.
She looked at Riya with cold smiling eyes.
Riya's expression transformed to match hers.

"At least my 'scrawny ass' reached 61 Quintillion without needing to hide behind the Council's pathetic complexity cap, Aunty Elina," she said sweetly. "How's that 50 Quintillion treating you? Still comfortable sitting down there?"
Elina's face pulsed, her aura buzzing with indignation.
"Why you little..."
"Enough."
Kael's voice cut through everything.
He floated forward!

"Ancestor," he said, turning to Noah while deliberately ignoring Riya, "this troublemaker should have told you a decent number of things by now. The Repository of Formed Authority and the Bastion of Mana represent just the beginning of what we've accomplished."

"With you in the lead, with your Infinite Mana guiding our efforts, what we can accomplish has become infinitely grander. We have systems, techniques, principles...all waiting for the final component that only you can provide."
Noah nodded, his tyrannical gaze sweeping across the assembled Seed Members.
"Yes," he said. "This is just the start. We will take what you all have accomplished here and bring another part of this Civilization...The Infiniverse, to reach this same height."
WAA!
He paused.
"They did not have the millions of years you all had. They have just
begun walking on the Way of Mana in the last day. But with the systems you've developed, with the Repositories and Glyphs you've
refined, we will compress their advancement timeline to match your own achievements."
Kael and the others showed expressions of astonishment.
Bringing an entire separate Civilization to their level in short period of
time? It was audacious to think of!
But this was the Ancestor speaking.
The one who'd given them Mana and told them to build something magnificent in isolation. If he said it could be done...
They nodded, their expressions transforming into determination.
Noah's voice took on commanding weight.
"Prepare the Repository of Formed Authority to transfer at least half
of all stored Glyphs here. And any other means of rapid elevation you all have designed...ready everything for immediate deployment."
Kael bowed deeply. "It will be done, Ancestor. We will-"
"You all take care of these minor things."
Riya stepped forward, her voice cutting through Kael's response.
"I'll take the Ancestor to the place I designed specifically for his advancement. Don't even try to follow, okay? I've blocked off all
access."
Her jewel-blue eyes sparkled with mischief.
Before anyone could respond, before Kael could voice the objection
already forming on his lips...
Riya moved.
HUUM!
Faster than anyone present could track, her form blurring with speed
that transcended their considerable perception.
Mana wrapped around both her and Noah in complex, and they
disappeared!
WHOOSH!
Kael's expression transformed into frustration once more.
Voltrax, Riya's father, materialized beside Kael with a slight smile, his hand raised in a calming gesture.
"Let's just do our part," he said, "You know how much Riya adored The
Stories of The Ancestor more than anything else. She probably memorized every detail you shared about him over the eons."
His smile widened slightly.
"Let her have her fill of his presence. She'll settle down afterwards

and become manageable again. Come on...let us prepare the aid packages for the advancement of the Ancestor's other part of Civilization. That's where we can actually contribute meaningfully." The others sighed collectively, their frustration dissipating into weary
acceptance.
They dispersed, floating toward different sections of the Repository to begin the massive undertaking of packaging millions of years of accumulated advancement for transfer!
Noah's vision cleared as the teleportation of Mana completed, and he
found himself standing atop one of the massive ring-shaped buildings that floated in the skies of this grand Civilization. Rivers of blue mana flowed through the air around them.
They cascaded past the building's edges and circled back through the
loops. Riya sat down on the building's surface, her legs dangling over the edge as she used her fingers to play with the flowing mana.
The blue currents responded to her touch like living things, wrapping
around her fingers, forming complex patterns at her silent direction. "For me," she said quietly, "when too many mana signatures cluster in one place, my sensitivity actually overloads my senses."
She manipulated the flowing mana into a spiral, watching it spin with distant focus.

"It's like... imagine if you could hear every individual conversation in a crowd, every breath, every heartbeat, every rustle of clothing...all at maximum volume, all demanding your attention simultaneously. That's what large gatherings feel like to me. Overwhelming.
Exhausting." Her jewel-blue eyes remained fixed on the mana spiral.
"I prefer purity. Singular, focused signatures rather than chaotic
clusters. That's why I've been taking you away from large crowds since you arrived. Not just to show off or be irreverent..." She paused, then looked at Noah directly.
"When it comes to purity, your existence gives off a sense that's
unmatched. Like... concentrated essence of mana itself, undiluted by any other authority. My sensitivity actually calms down around you.
Since you appeared, your existence has been drowning out the noise
of everyone else."
Bursts of rivers of Mana bloomed right after as this entire region became even more radiant!

clusters.
That's why I've been taking you away from large crowds since you arrived.
Not just to show off or be irreverent..." She paused, then looked at Noah directly.
"When it comes to purity, your existence gives off a sense that's
unmatched.
Like... concentrated essence of mana itself, undiluted by any other authority.
My sensitivity actually calms down around you.
Since you appeared, your existence has been drowning out the noise
of everyone else."
Bursts of rivers of Mana bloomed right after as this entire region became even more radiant!

chapters.title: Chapter 4384 The Civilization of Mana! V
paragraphs: Noah turned to face this anomaly fully, his perception focusing on her with renewed intensity.
She was much more complex than how she presented herself.
The sarcasm, the attitude...all of it masked something else.
He looked out at the vast Civilization spread below them, the floating structures and towers and millions of beings all carrying his Way of Existence.
"I thought of many possibilities that could arise from this Civilization," he said quietly. "Mutations. Changes in approach. Refinements of Glyphs, new Glyphs..."
His gaze returned to Riya.
"I did not expect an anomaly at your level."
She smiled at these words and nodded.
Then she sighed, her expression becoming more serious.
"I did say I was taking you to a place designed for your advancement," she said softly. "But really... you're looking at it. You're looking at her."
As she spoke those words, her body pulsed with sudden brilliance.
Around her form, the aura of glorious Principles bloomed into existence....and it was three distinct signatures of authority!
And each one blazed with concentrated essence of pure Mana. Noah's gaze sharpened immediately.
Riya stood slowly, her form radiating power as she gestured at the first Principle...a light that shone blue-gold, pulsing with rhythmic intensity.

"Principle exist in nature. We don't make them, we don't design them. We discover them, and we can maybe at most tweak them. Inside a Civilization built around Mana, I was able to discover, gain access to, and nurture Principles without having met the heavy requirements of The Way of The Mana Architect. I'm that fucking good, Ancestor." HUUM!
"This one," she said, "I call the Principle of Primus Ascension."
The blue-gold light intensified in response to her attention.

"When in an active state, this Principle enhances the flow, density, and potency of Mana by transforming it into Primus Mana...an elevated form that carries approximately 10 times the effectiveness of normal Mana in all applications."
Her jewel-blue eyes gleamed.

"Keeping this Principle active costs Mana continuously. For most beings, even those with vast reserves, maintaining it long-term would be prohibitively expensive. But for the legendary Ancestor who has Infinite Mana..."
She smiled knowingly.
"You'll simply get an all-around improvement with zero cost. Every technique, every Glyph, every application of your authority...all of it operating at 10x effectiveness permanently."
She paused, her expression becoming more serious.

"This Principle sits above Grand Principles in the hierarchy. Only I have access to it, with a single exception clause built into its fundamental nature: someone who possesses more Mana than me could theoretically claim it. Which was... impossible this whole time, right?"
Her smile turned mischievous.
"Until you arrived, Little Ancestor, with your Infinite Mana."
Noah stared at the blue-gold light.
'A Principle that elevates Mana to a superior form. It sits slightly below Perpetual Harvest in weight...'
He speculated as he gave it a thorough look, RUIN/EDEN's prompts already flashing in the background as she began to analyze
everything.
He was looking at the one who was able to nurture such a wonder by herself.
His fascination must have shown on his face, because Riya's smile widened before she gestured at the second Principle.
This one shone blue-purple, its light carrying a quality of dominance that made the surrounding mana instinctively orient itself toward the
glow.
"This one," Riya said, her voice taking on almost reverent tones, "I call the Principle of Mana Supremacy."
The blue-purple light pulsed with authority.

"Its function is straightforward but profound: the supremacy of Mana over all other weavings of Existence. It allows for the transformation of any authority...any concept, any power, any fundamental force...into Mana-based variations."
She gestured, and illusory examples bloomed around them.

"Living Existential Authority becomes Living Existential Mana Authority. Living Paradoxical Authority becomes Living Paradoxical Mana Authority. Living Quantum becomes Living Quantum Mana. Living Spirit becomes Living Spirit Mana."
Her eyes blazed with the weight of what she was describing.

"All variations of authority...every fundamental force, every conceptual framework, every power structure...transformed under the banner of Mana. The most grand depiction of supremacy and purity that Mana
can achieve."
She paused.

"This Principle sits above all other Grand Principles in terms of transformative capability, but it's still designated as such because key members of our Civilization could potentially obtain it. It's not singular like some others...it can be held by multiple beings, though the transformation it provides scales with the wielder's Existence."
Noah's mind pulsed with implications!
A Principle to alter everything under the banner of Mana!
Oh!
The thought cascaded through his consciousness.
'My core concepts...Veritarch, Quintessence, Tyranny, Cheats,
Protagonist... what would they become if reborn with Mana at their
fundamental core?"
"Tyrannical Mana Authority. Quintessential Mana Essence...'
The possibilities were endless!
Before he could fully process these implications, Riya continued,
gesturing at the third Principle.
This one's light was different...pure blue.
"And this one," Riya said, her voice dropping to become almost
solemn, "I call the Principle of Arcana Infinitum."
The pure blue light pulsed, and Noah felt appetite radiating from it.
The desire to transform, to convert, to break down and rebuild
according to specific parameters.
Riya's expression became intense as she explained.

"This Principle is meant to allow you to break down and devour anything for the sake of Mana advancement. Not just beings or resources....anything. Creatures that are 5 Quintillion Complexity and Purity below you? Normally they'd give you nothing meaningful. With this Principle, they can be burned as fuel to power your Way!"
She gestured broadly.
"All for the sake of smoothing out any hardships on this path. Forming

more and more Glyphs gets exponentially harder after the first 10,000, yes? Even with the Ancestor's Infinite Mana, there's a complexity ceiling where each new Glyph requires more time." Her jewel-blue eyes blazed.
"This Principle becomes the solution. Use everything around you as
fuel that will be directly applied to overcome that hardship of progression. Whether it be Existences, Resources, or even Folds themselves...all of it can be consumed and converted into
advancement toward your next Glyph, your next breakthrough."
She took a breath.
"Mana Arcana Glyphs are hard to design in an overpowered way? This

Principle acts as the knife to cut through those hardships, allowing you to forge whatever complex and terrifying Mana Arcana Glyph you want by consuming resources that provide the necessary understanding directly."
Her voice took on desperate weight.
"It's meant to be a knife to cut through any obstacle you might

encounter on the path to sufficient power. To ensure that no limitation...not complexity ceilings, not Glyph formation difficulties, not theoretical understanding gaps...can slow your advancement when time is the one resource we lack."
She paused, and something shifted in her expression.
"This Principle is Singular. Only one entity may hold it at any given
time. It's... it's mine currently, woven into my fundamental existence."
Tears began forming in her jewel-blue eyes, blue mana crystallizing into liquid that spilled down her cheeks.
"But I will give it up to you, Ancestor. After hearing all the legends
about you from Uncle Kael, after spending hundreds of thousands of
years refining this specifically for the moment you would return..."
Her voice broke.
"This is what I prepared for you. Please. Please, use it to save us all."
The tears flowed freely now, blue mana streaming down her face as her form trembled with emotion.
"Please!" she said again, her voice carrying the weight of nearly a
million years of desperate hope!
HUUM!
She continued through her crying, words tumbling out. "Ancestor, I don't want to lose my family. I don't want to lose my

father, Uncle Kael, everyone who's been with me for hundreds of thousands of years. Please, take all that you need and... guide us to the other side. Guide us through whatever catastrophe is coming. I'll give up anything...power, principles, my own advancement...just please don't let them disappear."
At such a pivotal moment, Noah moved.
He crossed the distance between them in a single step, his hand
reaching out to hold her head gently.
Due to their relative sizes, her head fit within his palm, and she
grabbed his hand instinctively as she looked up at him through tear-blurred vision.
She felt the immense warmth emanating from him. The weight of what he was washed over her like a tide of endless
potential. His Infinite Mana radiated through the contact, and it felt like being embraced by the ocean itself!
She trembled, then jumped into his full embrace, holding him tightly
as that endless warmth surrounded her completely.
And yet tears still fell from her eyes silently, blue Mana streaming down to disappear into the flowing currents around them.
"Ancestor," she said quietly against his chest, "I have a deep connection with Mana. My sensitivity allows me to sense its brilliance not just in the current time, but before and afterwards."
Her grip tightened.
"Mana has been bright in my gaze this whole time...brilliant, endless,
growing stronger with each passing year as our Civilization refined your Way. But..."
She trembled.
"I have felt the brilliance of Mana being dwindled and stifled in the
future. It terrified me. It affirmed that the catastrophe is very real,
that The Collapse is coming and will be devastating enough to extinguish even Mana's light."
At this moment, in his embrace, Riya raised her head to look directly into his eyes.
Tears continued streaming down her face as she looked heartbroken
and desperate.

"So I was waiting for you with eagerness and dread. Eager to finally meet the legendary Ancestor. Dreading that your arrival would confirm the catastrophe's proximity. But I hoped...desperately hoped, that after your appearance, the light of Mana would continue to shine
bright in my future perception. That your presence would change our fates." Her voice cracked.
"After showing you our Civilization. After presenting the Bastion of
Mana. After offering you these Principles that I've refined specifically
to ensure your survival, your advancement, your capability to save us
all..."
BOOM!
Her next words were unfathomably heavy! "Even now, I still sense the brightness of Mana flickering and dimming
in the future!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4385 Primus! I
paragraphs: Above a grand citadel of an advanced Civilization, the scene was very, very heavy!
Heartbroken and crying, Riya looked at Noah with an expression that contained millions of years of desperate hope collapsing into despair.

"Ancestor, why... why has it not changed? Why, after all this, after you've seen what we built, after I've given you tools specifically designed to ensure victory...why is the light of Mana still set to dim in my perception of what's coming?"
Her gaze at this moment felt immensely heavy!
She looked to him for answers when at this moment, he did not have any!
Why hasn't the future changed?
Noah embraced her tighter, his hand stroking her hair gently as he looked out at the vast Civilization spread around them.
The floating ring structures. The towers pulsing with accumulated power. The millions of beings carrying his Way.
All of it built through desperation and Mana into something magnificent.
And according to Riya's sensitivity...according to her unique perception of Mana across time...all of it was still destined to dim.

What could possibly accomplish that? Do we truly fail on all accounts? Does the Bastion of Mana not succeed? Do I fail to reach THE distinction before The Fallout arrives? Does something else... some variable I haven't accounted for...emerge to destroy everything despite all these preparations?
Just... what goes wrong?
His mind raced through possibilities, discarding unlikely scenarios, focusing on the factors that could genuinely threaten a Civilization of this magnitude.
THE Loom and its Justiciars. THE Dead Order and their response to his killing of their Prime Dead Early Creatures. THE Creature.
The fundamental Collapse of existence itself. Unknown variables operating on scales he hadn't yet perceived.
Any of those could be the source of Mana's dimming light in Riya's future perception.
Or perhaps multiple factors converging simultaneously, creating cascade failures that even his preparations couldn't prevent.
His own senses as the pioneer of this Civilization didn't tell him any of this.
But he couldn't just categorize the words of an anomaly like Riya as
untrue.
He looked down at her crying form, still clutched against his chest. What she feels should be valid.
Which meant despite everything...despite his advancement, despite the Isolated Civilization's achievements, despite the Bastion of Mana and these offered Principles...something was still wrong.
Some critical factor remained unaddressed.
Some threat existed that would dim Mana's light- his glorious, magisterial brilliance...despite all their preparations.
The question of exactly what echoed through his tyrannical mind.
How do I change a future that apparently hasn't shifted despite everything I've already done?
He held Riya tighter, his Infinite Mana flowing through their contact
in waves meant to comfort, to reassure, even as his mind continued calculating.
His ideology was one of Tyranny.
He did what he had to in ord to protect himself and his family.
He had built entire existence around many things, with being the
principle that...
Nothing was predetermined! Everything could be changed with sufficient audacity, tyranny, and Infinite Mana.
Even futures that apparently remained dark despite millions of years of desperate preparation.
He just needed to figure out what was missing.
What piece of the puzzle remained undiscovered.
His tyrannical heart pulsed with determination!
The Early Creature, Osmont, stood atop a floating ring structure, holding a prodigy who'd spent years preparing for his return, staring out at a Civilization that was somehow still destined to fail.
And he began planning how to violate that future as thoroughly as he'd violated every other limitation existence had tried to impose on
him!
He held Riya gently, his hand still stroking her hair as tears slowly stopped falling from her jewel-blue eyes.
His expression remained steady, his tyrannical composure unshaken!
"Do you feel," he asked quietly, "the immensity of the Mana burning
within me?"
Riya nodded silently, closing her eyes as her enhanced sensitivity reached out to truly perceive what he was.
An ocean without shores, a well without bottom, a flame that consumed nothing because it was the source itself. Mana that didn't
deplete or diminish or fade!
Noah continued.
"All I have ever had," he said, "has been that Mana. From the very beginning, when I first discovered what I was capable of, it has been the single constant in an existence defined by escalating
impossibilities."
His gaze drifted across the Civilization spread below them.
"And with it, I have gone through many apocalypses. Natural ones...
cosmic catastrophes, existential collapses, the death of entire realities. Engineered ones...beings who decided that existence needed
to end and possessed the power to make it happen. They're all the same at their core...overwhelming force seeking to unmake
everything."
"And while I cannot say why the dimming of Mana you feel has not

changed, why your perception of the future remains dark despite everything we've accomplished, I will continue to work toward a solution to overcome this apocalypse just like all those before it." He looked down at her, his tyrannical gaze meeting her tear-stained
face.

"I will continue to violate every limitation. To defy every predetermined outcome. To find paths forward where none should exist. That is what I do. That is what I am. And I will not stop until either we have changed that future you perceive. Okay?"
At these words, Riya nodded, remaining with her head against his
chest.

Her jewel-blue eyes twinkled with curiosity as she looked up at him. "How...did you solve the other apocalypses?" she asked softly. Noah blinked, the question pulling him into nostalgia for battles that felt simultaneously ancient and recent depending on which reference
frame he used.
"Brute force most of the time," he admitted.
"I become stronger than the apocalypse itself, or stronger than the
thing bringing forth the apocalypse. Overwhelm the threat with sufficient power that its apocalyptic nature becomes irrelevant."
He paused.
"That has been the goal for The Fallout as well. But when it's something set in motion such a long time ago, with beings operating on an entirely different Scale of Existence..."
"It is turning out to be just a little difficult."
A little difficult.
Hah!
Riya looked up at him, her expression shifting as decisiveness
replaced the despair that had dominated moments before. Her jewel-blue eyes pulsed with determination.
"Okay, Ancestor," she said, "I will give you my Everythi- "
Before she could finish, Noah shook his head.
"None of that," he said firmly. "I do not need my people to make
sacrifices for my gains."

to end and possessed the power to make it happen.
They're all the same at their core...overwhelming force seeking to unmake
everything."
"And while I cannot say why the dimming of Mana you feel has not

changed, why your perception of the future remains dark despite everything we've accomplished, I will continue to work toward a solution to overcome this apocalypse just like all those before it." He looked down at her, his tyrannical gaze meeting her tear-stained
face.
"I will continue to violate every limitation.
To defy every predetermined outcome.
To find paths forward where none should exist.
That is what I do.
That is what I am.
And I will not stop until either we have changed that future you perceive.
Okay?"
At these words, Riya nodded, remaining with her head against his
chest.
Her jewel-blue eyes twinkled with curiosity as she looked up at him.
"How...did you solve the other apocalypses?" she asked softly.
Noah blinked, the question pulling him into nostalgia for battles that felt simultaneously ancient and recent depending on which reference
frame he used.
"Brute force most of the time," he admitted.
"I become stronger than the apocalypse itself, or stronger than the
thing bringing forth the apocalypse.
Overwhelm the threat with sufficient power that its apocalyptic nature becomes irrelevant."
He paused.
"That has been the goal for The Fallout as well.
But when it's something set in motion such a long time ago, with beings operating on an entirely different Scale of Existence..."
"It is turning out to be just a little difficult."
A little difficult.
Hah!
Riya looked up at him, her expression shifting as decisiveness
replaced the despair that had dominated moments before.
Her jewel-blue eyes pulsed with determination.
"Okay, Ancestor," she said, "I will give you my Everythi- "
Before she could finish, Noah shook his head.
"None of that," he said firmly.
"I do not need my people to make
sacrifices for my gains."

chapters.title: Chapter 4386 Primus! II
paragraphs: The words caused Riya's eyes to shine.
She rose on her tiptoes, her hands reaching forward to wrap around his neck as her nose and lips came within inches of his.
At this proximity, her enhanced sensitivity to Mana made her tremble with the sheer presence of his Infinite reserves.
She looked directly into his eyes, her expression transforming into something playful and serious simultaneously.

"Then I will just give you my Heart," she said softly. "It's fucking delicate, like a little tiny crystal. You are the only one who may be worth it in my existence, and I am a little arrogant by nature so..."
Her smile widened.
"You will have time to earn it in the future. One of my plans, Ancestor, is a devilish one. It is to make you ridiculously obsessed with me and my Primus Mana to the point that losing me would be so
unimaginably painful that... you will do everything you can to ensure we survive The Fallout."
Her jewel-blue eyes sparkled with mischief.
"It's a win-win for me. By the end, I will have you wrapped around my fingers. So I will apologize about this in advance, Little Ancestor."
Her words were bold, and her lips brushed against his with every syllable.
Noah looked at her with an expression that suggested he viewed her as a poor thing who had no idea what she'd just gotten herself into.
Without wasting a moment, Riya pushed off her tiptoes and her lips fully connected with his.
And...
BOOM!
A singularity of Mana bloomed between them.
On Riya's side, she felt like she had connected to a boundless sun of Mana that she had always dreamed of touching.
It was so pure, so pristine...not diluted by any other authority, not mixed with inferior elements, just concentrated essence of what Mana could be at its absolute peak.
Naturally, the first thing she did after sensing access to this infinite sea was simple.
'Eat it all up!'
Her closed eyes flashed with fierce hunger as she drank the heat of his Infinite Mana endlessly, as if she wanted to experience what it would be like to hold endless reserves herself.
Her sensitivity allowed her to perceive and absorb with efficiency others could not imagine.
On Noah's side, he felt an extremely pure source of Mana connect to him, Riya's refined essence, polished through years of isolated cultivation.
It tapped into his Infinite reserves excitedly and hungrily, drinking as if she would be shut out soon when really, she needed to pace herself or risk overwhelming herself.
He would let her have her fun for now.
Because the presents she was gifting him were far too grand to deny.
No, he did not need her to sacrifice her Principles for him.
Those who constantly require sacrifices from others to achieve anything on their behalf are not truly following The Way.
The thought settled into his consciousness.
They are parasites wearing the mask of pioneers. They take from

those beneath them and call it leadership. They demand offerings and name it guidance. But to truly follow The Way, to pioneer it as I intend to...one must try their best to lead without requiring sacrifices.
To elevate others through one's own strength rather than depleting them for temporary gains.
His eyes flashed with a glorious light as he thought of this!
And so, even as Riya drank deeply from his Infinite reserves, Noah made a decision.
'Cheating Architect. Perpetual Harvest!
He called out to his Singularity Principles with focused intent, his consciousness touching the fundamental architecture of what they represented.

'Award the effort of Riya and this Civilization. Recognize their advancement. Harvest what they have accomplished and integrate it into our shared Way. She will not be losing access to any of her Singularity Principles'
BOOOOOM!
An even larger explosion of Mana erupted from their connection.
In the skies above the Isolated Civilization, millions of beings raised their heads to witness a phenomenon.
A massive singularity bloomed overhead...the purest Mana they had ever perceived, condensed to the point where it became visible even to those without enhanced sensitivity.
But it didn't shine pure blue.
It blazed blue-gold.
Primus Mana, the elevated form that Riya had spent years refining
into existence.
They all gazed toward it in awe, many falling to their knees
instinctively as the blue-gold sun became utterly blinding.
Children pointed and asked questions their parents couldn't answer. Researchers scrambled to record readings. The Council Members felt their own Mana resonate!
The Ancestor's presence had transformed into something more.
Meanwhile, within Noah's mind, a cascade of prompts bloomed en
masse.
CRITICAL DISCOVERY - PRINCIPLE INTEGRATION DETECTED
Classification: 2 Singularity Principles + 1 Grand Principle
Source: External Cultivation - Isolated Civilization Member (Riya)|
PRINCIPLES IDENTIFIED:|
-Principle of Primus Ascension (Singularity)|
|-Principle of Arcana Infinitum (Singularity)|
-Principle of Mana Supremacy (Grand)|
Direct connection established with the existence who nurtured these
Principles to maturity. Analyzing compatibility...
COMPATIBILITY ASSESSMENT: EXCEPTIONAL
The connection is extremely in tune with your Way of Existence.
These Principles operate on frameworks that align seamlessly with your established architecture. Countless processes have been made
easier through integration.
PRINCIPLE OF PRIMUS ASCENSION - DETAILED ANALYSIS:

Backdoor access code detected within Principle's fundamental structure. Analysis suggests intentional design...this Principle was built to be claimed by an existence possessing Infinite Mana. Riya's architectural modifications include exception clause: "Any existence whose Mana reserves exceed the Principle holder's by
infinite magnitude may claim this authority without conflict."] PRINCIPLE STATUS: Already nurtured and bloomed to full maturity]
INTEGRATION COMMENCING...|
The Principle of Primus Ascension is now spreading across your existence. All Mana within your being is undergoing elevation to
Primus state.
At this moment, within Noah's inner existence, the mental landscape where his consciousness could observe his own architectural framework...the familiar scene manifested with new additions.
An endless seascape of blue stretched in all directions, the ocean of
his Infinite Mana given visual representation. Standing on that ocean's surface, RUIN/EDEN's illusory form appeared alongside Noah's humanoid mental projection.
In the distance, two massive trees rose from the blue sea.
The first blazed with vibrant green-gold light...the Principle of Perpetual Harvest, its branches heavy with fruits of accumulated effort, its roots drinking deep from the ocean of Mana beneath.
The second shone with pure gold radiance...the Principle of Cheating Architect.
RUIN/EDEN waved her hands, and the seascape shifted.
A third tree rose from the blue ocean, this one shining with brilliant
blue-gold luminescence.
The Principle of Primus Ascension.
Its form was elegant, almost crystalline, each branch and leaf
constructed from what looked like compressed theorems of Mana elevation.
All Mana within your being- every particle, every quantum of power,
every reserve both active and latent, is undergoing elevation to Primus state.
This is not a temporary enhancement. This is permanent restructuring of your foundational energy architecture.| Due to this pivotal change, much of the authority of this Principle
was clustered here. It may hold fewer ultimate features or locked
features.
Tracking changes now...
Noah felt it happening in real-time.
The endless blue of his existence, the ocean of Infinite Mana that
defined what he was...began to transform.

His Mana was gaining grander qualities. Becoming denser in the sense of information density. Each unit of Primus Mana carried more potential, more capability, more fundamental weight than normal Mana could hold.
Becoming purer...not cleaner, because his Mana had always been
pure, but refined.
It was necoming more complex, more sophisticated. The interactions between Mana particles were becoming more intricate.
Which meant that his Complexity and Purity parameters...the measurements of his existential weight, were beginning to transform
as well!
His Mana was becoming something more. Something unfathomably more!

chapters.title: Chapter 4387 Primus! III
paragraphs: Noah's mind engaged fully, trying to understand what Primus Mana represented at fundamental levels.
When normal Mana powers a technique, it's like combusting gasoline- efficient, predictable, well-understood.
When Primus Mana powers that same technique, it's like initiating fusion reactions...orders of magnitude more energy from the same apparent volume, with entirely different interactions!
The transformation was qualitative.
Activating a Mana Glyph of Primordial Fireball with normal Mana creates flames that follow established parameters-temperature, volume, destructive potential all calculable.
Activating that same Glyph with Primus Mana...
His mind raced.
The flames wouldn't just be hotter or larger. The flames could burn Concepts, Living Existential Authority, Early Existential Authority...
The flames of his Glyphs may become capable of even burning the light of Principles themselves!
And for something complex like a Mana Arcana Glyph of the Primordial Mana-Flame Wyrm...
The construct would be more real, existing with greater solidity,

greater autonomy, greater capability to affect existence because every particle of Mana forming it carried enhanced weight. A Primordial Primus Mana-Flame Wyrm could potentially exist for seconds, minutes, or hours...
The transformation continued spreading through his being, and Noah felt systems he'd established beginning to complete.
The elevation of your Mana to Primus state has triggered cascade
completion across multiple systems:
SERAPHILIC VEINLACE: 100% Integration Complete
INCARNAUT SANCTIS: 100% Integration Completel
CHAMBER OF BLOOD: Fundamental Architecture Restructured
Previous Capacity: 9 Mana-Born Early Creatures
New Capacity: 729 Mana-Born Early Creatures]
Explanation: Primus Mana allows for vastly more sophisticated transformations.
HUUM!
Noah's consciousness pulsed!
729 transformations instead of 9!
And RUIN/EDEN wasn't finished!
A Grand Milestone Has Been Achieved.
THE HEART OF THE EARLY CREATURE, OSMONT: COMPLETE
HUUM!
The words blazed across his consciousness.
Your Heart has been fully formed.
Analysis: The "Heart" in this context is not the biological organ, but the existential core, the fundamental anchor point that defines what you are rather than what you do.
For Early Creatures, the Heart represents the completed integration of all foundational systems into a unified whole. It is the moment when scattered elements of power coalesce into genuine identity.
Previous State: You were a collection of advanced systems operating in coordination
Current State: You are a unified existence with those systems as expressions of your nature
The distinction matters existentially. You are no longer becoming The
Early Creature.
You ARE The Early Creature.]
The final line carried profound weight!
Your Existence can now truly begin.
WAA!
Noah stood in his mental seascape, RUIN/EDEN beside him, three Principle-trees rising from the infinite blue ocean that was
transforming to blue-gold before his eyes.
And two more were about to bloom.
And... he felt complete in ways he hadn't even realized he'd been incomplete before.
His Heart, his existential core, had finished forming.
Everything he'd built, every system he'd established, every Principle
he'd cultivated, all of it had finally integrated into a unified whole that
was greater than the sum of its parts.
He was no longer just Noah.
He was The Early Creature, Osmont.
Now, he just needed THE.
And his existence, properly formed at last, could now truly begin
whatever came next.

In the external world, Riya continued drinking from his Infinite reserves, unaware that what she consumed had transformed mid-connection from normal Mana into Primus Mana, she simply felt like a drunkard whose drink had become even sweeter.
The blue-gold sun blazing above the Isolated Civilization pulsed brighter, painting vast swathes of existence in enhanced authority. And Noah, The Early Creature, Osmont, with his Heart finally
complete and his Mana elevated to Primus state...his voice began to echo out even while lips were sealed by an anomaly.
His voice boomed from his Existence.
From his Heart!
His voice echoed out across the Isolated Civilization, and because it
was no longer isolated, his voice shockingly spread out across the
Wandering Territories!
"I defy, therefore I exist."
WAA!
"I refuse limitations, therefore I transcend."
HUUM!
"I cultivate infinity, therefore...I need not fear the end."
BOOM!
His eyes blazed with blue-gold light as he looked out across his
Civilization.
His words echoed and echoed grandly!
Across his Civilization!
Across the Wandering Territories!
His voice filled with Primus Mana, dense and filled with majesty,
leaked out and rang out even across the distant Transcendent Folds
of Living Existences!
His voice...passed across The Veil to enter the side where The Dead
thrived!
The Great Usurper, whose existence held an intricate connection with him, was roused out of his idleness as he blinked in
astonishment!
Oh!
I defy, therefore I exist!
I refuse limitations, therefore I transcend!
I cultivate infinity, therefore...I need not fear the end!
Such words echoed out across existence at this moment.
And Existence took some time to let it settle.
And those who heard it were forced to stop, listen, and ponder!
It was a pivotal moment in time.
Within Noah's mental seascape.
His existence calmed from thr exuberance of what he had just uttered
while continuing its silent but heavy transformation.
RUIN/EDEN's illusory form shifted position, moving toward the newly manifested blue-gold tree that pulsed with rhythmic brilliance.
The Principle of Primus Ascension.
"Master, the Principle of Primus Ascension is now ready for analysis.
Shall we examine its comprehensive capabilities?"
Noah's mental projection nodded, his attention focusing entirely on what more this new Principle could provide after the simple but critical change from Mana to Primus Mana its authority was focused
into.
RUIN/EDEN raised one hand, and the space around the blue-gold tree transformed into cascading displays of data and possibility. PRINCIPLE OF PRIMUS ASCENSION - FULL INTEGRATION
ANALYSIS
Core Functionality: Mana Elevation Architecture Foundational Effect: All Mana within Master's existence and sphere of
influence operates at Primus state...a qualitatively superior form carrying approximately 10x effectiveness across all applications.
The displays then shifted, showing intricate patterns of Mana flow between multiple connected existences. Additional Primary Ability: [Primus Bestowal]]
Function: One can grant temporary or permanent Primus Mana
conversion to 729 existences within your Civilization's architectural framework, but they have to bear the cost with Primus Mana.
Temporary Duration: 1 hour to 7 days, scaling with recipient's
compatibility
Permanent Conversion: Requires direct physical contact and conscious acceptance from recipient. Once converted, their Mana permanently operates at Primus state.
Civilization Application: This creates a cascading elevation effect.
Each Citizen granted permanent Primus conversion becomes a node of enhanced capability. Their advancement accelerates by factor of 10. Their techniques become qualitatively superior. Their complexity
ceiling increases substantially. Systematic conversion of your Civilization's population would elevate
average power levels tremendously.
Noah's perception focused on this capability with intense interest as another rose up.
Secondary Ability: [Primus Resonance Field]]

Function: Master can establish a geographical zone where all Mana automatically operates at Primus state regardless of source. Current Range: Length of Early Veiled Shore Effect Within Range: Any being utilizing Mana-based abilities experiences 10x enhancement. Your Civilization members receive full
benefit.]
"And finally," RUIN/EDEN said, "the ultimate expression of this Principle."
Ultimate Ability: [Primus Singularity]]
Function: Once per significant temporal period, Master can designate
a specific existence as a Primus Singularity, a point where Mana concentration and quality reach theoretical maximums.

Duration: Approximately 1 hour at current complexity Effect Within Singularity: All Mana-based advancement operates at 100x normal efficiency. Breakthroughs that would require decades occur in minutes. Cultivation that would span lifetimes compresses
into hours.
Personal Application: Designate your own existence as Primus Singularity during critical advancement attempts. Compress the path
to THE distinction into achievable timeframes.
RUIN/EDEN stepped back slightly.
"The synergies with your existing Principles are substantial," she

added. "Perpetual Harvest amplifies every advancement occurring within Primus environments. Cheating Architect allows manipulation of Primus Mana's fundamental properties for customized effects. The three Principles create multiplicative rather than additive enhancement. I am still pocking around for its locked features if there are any."
The Principle was a glorious one. But even Singularity Principles seemed to have their own exceptionality as his own remained magisterial!

RUIN/EDEN raised one hand, and the space around the blue-gold tree transformed into cascading displays of data and possibility.

ANALYSIS
Core Functionality: Mana Elevation Architecture Foundational Effect: All Mana within Master's existence and sphere of
influence operates at Primus state...a qualitatively superior form carrying approximately 10x effectiveness across all applications.
The displays then shifted, showing intricate patterns of Mana flow between multiple connected existences.
Additional Primary Ability: [Primus Bestowal]]
Function: One can grant temporary or permanent Primus Mana
conversion to 729 existences within your Civilization's architectural framework, but they have to bear the cost with Primus Mana.
Temporary Duration: 1 hour to 7 days, scaling with recipient's
compatibility
Permanent Conversion: Requires direct physical contact and conscious acceptance from recipient.
Once converted, their Mana permanently operates at Primus state.
Civilization Application: This creates a cascading elevation effect.
Each Citizen granted permanent Primus conversion becomes a node of enhanced capability.
Their advancement accelerates by factor of 10.
Their techniques become qualitatively superior.
Their complexity
ceiling increases substantially.
Systematic conversion of your Civilization's population would elevate
average power levels tremendously.
Noah's perception focused on this capability with intense interest as another rose up.
Secondary Ability: [Primus Resonance Field]]
Function: Master can establish a geographical zone where all Mana automatically operates at Primus state regardless of source.
Current Range: Length of Early Veiled Shore Effect Within Range: Any being utilizing Mana-based abilities experiences 10x enhancement.
Your Civilization members receive full
benefit.]
"And finally," RUIN/EDEN said, "the ultimate expression of this Principle."
Ultimate Ability: [Primus Singularity]]
Function: Once per significant temporal period, Master can designate
a specific existence as a Primus Singularity, a point where Mana concentration and quality reach theoretical maximums.
Duration: Approximately 1 hour at current complexity Effect Within Singularity: All Mana-based advancement operates at 100x normal efficiency.
Breakthroughs that would require decades occur in minutes.
Cultivation that would span lifetimes compresses
into hours.
