sentences.text: As Noah bellowed such declarations into his own fundamental Existence, his eyes snapped open wide.
He gazed at Khor, who was watching him with mounting concern.
What she saw made her ancient composure falter as she knew about Ways of Existence a great deal.
She knew about their critical
singularity!
At this moment...
One of Noah's eyes radiated blue-gold tendrils of light...Primus Mana given visual form, cascading from his pupil like liquid brilliance.
The other pulsed with crimson-obsidian light...Hunger manifesting as darkness that devoured surrounding illumination while somehow remaining visible.
Mana.
Hunger.
Two fundamental forces operating through single existence, and somehow not destroying each other in the process.
At this moment, those impossible eyes locked onto Khor as Noah spoke.
And his voice...
Oh!
His voice boomed with unnatural depth and weight, as if it was emanating from a being that far exceeded everyone present.
Not louder, but heavier, carrying existential mass that made reality itself vibrate!
"Tell me of the Doctrines of Hunger I have not heard," he commanded, each word resonating across multiple dimensional frequencies.
"Tell me of the Fourth, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth Doctrines."
HUUM!
The declaration made the surrounding Mana and emerging Hunger ripple in immensity.
Khor looked at him with immense concern, her ancient eyes recognizing something profoundly dangerous in what he was attempting.
"Outsider," she said seriously, "are you sure of this?
What you're attempting..."
She asked, but Noah only gazed at her calmly with his mismatched eyes...one Mana, one Hunger, and spoke again with that impossible depth.
"Tell me of the other Doctrines of Hunger."
The repetition carried finality that clearly stated he would not be dissuaded.
After such unwavering affirmation, Khor nodded slowly, recognizing stubborn determination that mirrored her own ancient nature.
She began to recite.
"The Fourth Doctrine of Hunger states that Hunger thrives on impossibilities.
We do not hunger for what is easily obtained...such consumption provides no satisfaction.
We hunger for what should be beyond our reach, for what reality claims we cannot devour.
The more impossible the target, the more our Hunger sharpens.
Impossibility is not barrier but invitation.
When existence declares something cannot be consumed, Hunger hears only challenge."
Noah's existence buzzed with recognition as he nodded, understanding settling into his Existence!
Khor continued without pause.
"The Fifth Doctrine of Hunger states that Hunger enables infinite
growth.
There is no ceiling to what can be consumed, no limit to how vast Hunger can become.
Where other Ways encounter barriers and plateaus, Hunger simply devours those limitations and continues expanding.
We grow not despite obstacles but through them, consuming every ceiling until nothing remains to constrain our appetite.
Growth is not gradual, it is ravenous."
WAA!
Again Noah nodded, his mismatched eyes blazing brighter.
"The Sixth Doctrine of Hunger states that Hunger finds pleasure in consumption itself, not merely results.
We do not devour solely for power gained, we devour because the act of consumption brings profound satisfaction.
The journey of Hunger matters as much as the destination.
Every bite, every absorption, every integration carries its own joy.
This makes Hunger sustainable where pure ambition burns out."
Khor's voice gained intensity as she approached the final teachings.
"The Seventh Doctrine of Hunger states that Hunger transforms everything it touches into itself.
We do not simply accumulate, we convert.
Everything consumed becomes Hunger, everything devoured adds to our nature rather than diluting it.
A thousand different essences consumed do not create chaos but unified expansion.
Through Hunger, diversity becomes singular magnificent appetite."
She paused before the penultimate doctrine, her crimson eyes meeting Noah's impossible gaze.
"The Eighth Doctrine of Hunger states that Hunger must be shared to reach ultimate heights.
Solitary consumption creates powerful individuals, but shared Hunger creates Civilizations.
When multiple beings hunger together, when appetites align and consumption becomes coordinated, the resulting force transcends individual capability.
We do not compete for food, we feast together, and in that communion, become greater than any lone devourer could achieve."
BOOM!
After listening to each doctrine, Noah's existence processed and
integrated everything.
He closed his eyes, arms spreading wide as his body began gushing
even more concentrated waves of power.
Behind him, Ozymandias's figure manifested fully.
Their backs faced each other, two bodies sharing single
consciousness, and both began to spin.
Slowly at first, then accelerating, creating a vortex of mixed authorities that painted the sky in impossible colors.
The pressure Noah radiated was immense, the weight of someone forcing reality to accommodate what shouldn't be possible.
His voice boomed out again with that heavy, multi-dimensional depth, his voice seeming soft as he affirmed what he said before.
"My Way of Mana is unbreakable.
Infinite resources, endless refinement, systematic elevation...it cannot be diminished or destroyed.
My Way of Hunger is inevitable.
All things can be consumed, all limitations devoured, all growth enabled through appetite.
These truths are...fundamental."
His spinning accelerated.
"So my Existence...will simply have to make way and accept it."
BOOM!
The declaration hit reality like hammer striking anvil, and existence
complied.
What the fuck else could it do?!
HUUM!
Noah's body pulsed and radiated resplendent blue-gold brilliance...Primus Mana elevated to such concentration it became
nearly solid, painting half the sky in radiance that made observers
squint.

impossible forces.

Her jewel-blue gaze tracked between his forms with analytical intensity, trying to comprehend what was happening at existential levels in ways others could not see.
But her eyes saw much, much more than others.
Khor maintained somber expression as she observed radiant light of Hunger wrapping around him...around part of him, at least.
Her ancient eyes recognized what this meant, what doors were opening, what impossibilities were being enacted.
At such a moment, in the midst of all this glorious phenomena...

chapters.title: Chapter 4398 The Doctrines of Hunger V
paragraphs: The Early Infinity Dominion Realm.

Noah smiled internally as he thought of this self-proclaimed classification...even when he'd declared it what seemed like forever ago when it had only been days in objective time, he'd wondered if he would actually reach its gates.
And here I stand at its threshold. At the end of this self-proclaimed Realm... could be THE. Could be. Maybe.
Or I could be wrong, and THE distinction exists so far beyond this that my estimations were laughably inadequate...
There were countless possibilities!
His existence continued feeling waves of exuberance washing through every particle of his being...as if he was being baptized by currents of impossible coolness that brought unfathomable clarity.
Unfathomable clearness, as if fog he hadn't realized existed was being systematically burned away.
|You can now enact the weavings of both THE CIVILIZATION OF HUNGER and THE CIVILIZATION OF MANA|
|Your unique nature allows personal harmonization but cannot be transferred. Those within your respective Civilizations cannot be like you.|
|Due to emergence of your Two Ways of Existence and entry into The Early Infinity Dominion Realm:|
|The Lens of Civilization has bloomed within your existence. A unique viewpoint. A unique perspective.|
|—Perceive truths of Ways of Existence and Civilizations with enhanced clarity|
|—See through surface appearances to understand fundamental frameworks|
|—Read truths and inner thoughts of Hearts belonging to Moderately Complex and Minor Complex Existences|
|—Potential to see truth about yourself if proficiency develops sufficiently|
|—Enhanced analysis of enemy Civilizations.|
A terrifying capability bloomed within Noah's consciousness.
The Lens of Civilization.
An entry gift of the founding of Two Ways of Existence and entry into The Early Infinity Dominion Realm!
He sensed his existence brighten even more, as if he'd been gazing at everything through murky glass before and someone had suddenly cleaned it to crystal clarity.

His Complexity and Purity...which had been rising nonstop since altering his Mana to Primus state...seemed clearer now. Not just numbers increasing, but understanding of what those numbers meant, how they interacted with his fundamental nature, why certain thresholds mattered while others were arbitrary.
He could see his own existence with greater clarity. Understand his own mechanisms better!
What happens when I turn this Lens toward others? Toward their Civilizations? Toward THE entities when I finally encounter them directly?
Can I perceive the weaknesses in THE Dead Order's True Order? Identify flaws in THE Loom's defensive architecture? See through THE Living Paradox's carefully constructed machinations?
The implications cascaded through his mind!

He opened his eyes fully...both now returned to blue-gold, the crimson-obsidian having settled into Ozymandias exclusively, and felt profound change slowly settling over his existence like a new skin that fit perfectly despite never having worn it before.
Around him, his Isolated Civilization watched with expressions ranging from awe to concern to confusion.
Riya floated closer, her irreverence temporarily suspended by genuine curiosity.
"Ancestor," she said quietly, "what... what are you now? I can sense you're still you, but also... more? Different? My sensitivity to Mana is going haywire trying to classify what you've become."
Noah looked at her, and through The Lens of Civilization, he saw.
Her Heart, not the physical organ but the existential core.
Her deepest conviction...'protect what I love at any cost.'
Her hidden fear: 'that even infinite preparation won't be enough.'
Her secret hope: 'that this baddie of an Ancestor might actually change the dimming future she perceives'.
He blinked, startled by the sudden invasion of understanding he hadn't consciously sought.
And there was more he could do if he probed deeper!
He smiled at Riya.
"I am what I've always been," he said simply. "Just... more so."
Behind him, Ozymandias's form pulsed with synchronized agreement.
Two Ways. One Existence.
And Existence, for all its resistance, had finally accepted that this was possible!
With these two Ways of Existence and entrance into The Early Infinity Dominion Realm...
Even his Complexity and Purity had yet to settle with their advancement, the numbers still climbing, still integrating the profound changes coursing through his being.
Noah knew he also needed to define the precise parameters of his self-proclaimed realm, establish what exactly The Early Infinity Dominion Realm would entail.

But all of these were grand changes accumulating too rapidly, and in addition to everything else, there was Khor...whom he had not fully analyzed to quantify her new level of strength after the Existential Rollback.

With all these transformations...Two Ways harmonized, Primus Mana coursing through everything, The Lens of Civilization bloomed, entry into a new realm of power...has anything actually changed from what Riya perceived?
The question weighed heavily despite his recent triumphs.
He looked toward Riya, his mismatched eyes now returned to unified blue-gold meeting her jewel-blue gaze.
"Any... changes?" he asked simply.
His voice emanated with magnetic quality that seemed layered, coming in from different dimensions simultaneously.

Riya blinked, initially confused by the vague question. She stared into his complex eyes, trying to parse what he was asking, what specific aspect among countless recent developments he wanted her to assess.
Then understanding dawned, and her expression shifted.

Without a word, she closed her eyes, her enhanced sensitivity to Mana reaching outward and forward, perceiving not just the present but future trajectories, the brightness of Mana as it would exist in times yet to come.
A moment passed. Then another.
When she opened her eyes, her expression was downcast as she shook her head lightly.
"No changes," she said quietly.
She then looked at Kael and the others as she sent a silent mental note only for Noah to hear as she could not let the others know.
'I still sense the brilliant light of Mana dimming in the future. Everything you've accomplished hasn't altered what I perceive coming.'
Noah looked at her silently, his tyrannical composure absorbing that truth without visible reaction.
He nodded once, then turned to look toward Khor.
Before he could even formulate the question, she raised her hands, allowing obsidian-crimson darkness to coalesce over her fingers like living shadow.
"Your restoration and rollback of my existence was... somewhat useful, Outsider," she said lightly.
"I gained, or really, recovered, some memories. Uniquely, all of them seem like bad memories just from their taste alone."
Her crimson eyes flickered with something between pain and rage.

"These memories seem like something entirely new even for me, as I have not consciously gone through them. They feel like gaps being filled, spaces in my history that were surgically removed and are now bleeding back into awareness."

chapters.title: Chapter 4399 You! I
paragraphs: Khor paused, her expression hardening.
"I will display one which may be of importance for all of us to observe. It should be a memory of my existence...during or after my collapse."
She waved her hands, and a radiant, extremely solid illusory screen materialized in the air before them... a concentrated construct of her recovered Hunger given visual form.
After manifesting the screen, Khor closed her eyes, and on the illusory surface, obsidian darkness gave way to brilliance as a glorious...and horrifying scene began to play out.
Noah and the others watched as devastation bloomed across the screen.
The scene showed a fractured and decimated landscape of obsidian crystals stretching for impossible distances.
Billions upon billions of corpses...tentacled Inevitabilities in their natural forms, sprawled across the shattered crystalline terrain in poses suggesting violent, sudden death.
No signs of battle. Just... termination. As if something had simply decided they should cease existing and reality had complied.
In the center of all this devastation, the corpse of an adult Khor could be seen.

Her figure of sublime beauty seemed utterly defiled...an immense, massive gash permeated from her forehead vertically all the way down across her body, as if something had attempted to split her in half and had succeeded.
She was clearly dead. Unmistakably collapsed. Her existence terminated!
And standing over her corpse was a shadowy humanoid figure shrouded in darkness that made perception struggle to focus properly.
The entity was whistling nonchalantly...actually whistling, as if surveying the scene of genocide was a pleasant afternoon activity.
He reached out into Khor's corpse with familiarity and pulled, extracting a radiant obsidian-crimson Heart that pulsed with terrifying luminosity even in death.
The entity hummed while throwing the Heart up and down, feeling its weight with assessment.

"Another piece of the puzzle obtained..." he murmured with satisfaction, and he turned towards the corpse of Khor as he used his other hand to shut her absent crimson eyes tenderly, as if he was soothing her to sleep!
Noah's gaze hardened as he watched, his enhanced perception through The Lens of Civilization trying to pierce the shadows shrouding the figure.
Beside him in the present, Khor's eyes remained closed, but her hands were clenched so tightly her knuckles had gone white.
Her expression showed barely controlled rising lividity.
In the scene, three figures appeared behind the humanoid shadowy entity holding the Heart of Hunger.
They spoke in perfect unison, their voices overlapping.
"With this action, we must move even more quickly."
The humanoid entity shrouded in darkness nodded while continuing his humming.
"Yes, yes, My Little Weavers," he said.

"The Death of THE First Hunger will be felt by THE Creature. That guy has always looked after her from afar with sentimentality ever since he butchered her Master in a haze, and has wanted to make amends since. Ah... sentimentality of fools. Well, no matter."
He tossed the Heart casually.
"It is time to activate Anaximander against THE Creature. Do you have everything ready on your end?"
Noah's eyes flashed with chilling light as he processed those words.
THE Living Paradox and those three should be...THE Weavers. They're discussing using Anaximander as a weapon against THE Creature?!
His mind raced through possibilities while the scene continued!

THE Weavers replied in their unified voice: "It took considerable work, but Anaximander is prepared to be unleashed against THE Creature. He does not even comprehend what exactly he is doing, and he will not understand until the very last moment."
At such words, the shadowy figure grasping Khor's Heart of Hunger nodded as he turned.
And his face became clear in the scene.
"Let's get started!" he declared with enthusiasm that bordered on mania.
BOOM!
The moment his face became fully visible, Noah's eyes opened with shock.
In front of him in the present, Khor's eyes snapped open simultaneously, shock and lividity warring across her features as she howled!
That face!
They knew that face intimately!
She had recognized it before, and she had stated so!
BOOM!
An eruption of Hunger exploded where Khor stood, obsidian-crimson flames consuming the surrounding space as her eyes blazed with rage!
Noah stared at the face with a heavy gaze.
It was unfathomable. Impossible. And yet undeniable.
The face that THE Living Paradox was wearing in that memory...
Was the face of Schrodinger.
How? How could this be?
Noah's eyes flashed sharply as he looked at countless possibilities as...it did not make too much sense!
The beggar paradox, the Elderborn...he's THE Living Paradox? Or connected to him? A fragment? A Will? A disguise?
Khor's figure trembled with palpable rage, her voice shaking with barely restrained violence.
"I recognized him," she said, "I should have known! All this time...right under my nose!"
HUUM!
Her aura exploded outward.
"He collapsed billions of Inevitabilities! He collapsed MY existence and took my Heart of Hunger, my Primacy of Hunger! He enslaved all Inevitabilities and mutated them to work for his Loom! He..."
Her voice cracked with emotion!
"He must collapse! He must pay!"
BOOM!
Hunger began raging uncontrollably around her, obsidian-crimson flames consuming atmosphere itself.
Noah stepped forward, his voice holsing authority meant to penetrate her fury.
"Wait. Let us plan first. We cannot simply-"
But in the next moment...
WAP!
Khor disappeared.
Simply gone, as if she'd decided to exist somewhere else right away.
Noah's face became heavier with profound concern.
There were still too many unknowns!
If THE Living Paradox is truly Schrodinger, or potentially his Remnant Will, or some fragment, or something others can't even conceptualize...how powerful is he truly?
Going to face a being with THE distinction currently will have catastrophic consequences!
But Khor had already set off, and Noah felt what she felt through their brief connection during the memory viewing.
When it came to Hunger, the one quality he now understood intimately was this...whatever Hunger craved with sufficient potency, it would find.

Even if Khor didn't know precisely where Schrodinger was...though she did, because they'd been keeping tabs, with Schrodinger and Leonore currently hidden while observing a Justiciar complete its massacre in the Transcendent Quantum Folds with Noah's false illusions.
Even if she didn't know, her Hunger would track him and all his other bodies with inexorable certainty.
And she had already departed in her rage without questioning whether what they saw was truth, without wondering if they could actually face an existence with THE distinction at this moment.
Hunger was filled with fury!

WAP!
Khor disappeared.
Simply gone, as if she'd decided to exist somewhere else right away.
Noah's face became heavier with profound concern.
There were still too many unknowns!
If THE Living Paradox is truly Schrodinger, or potentially his Remnant Will, or some fragment, or something others can't even conceptualize...how powerful is he truly?
Going to face a being with THE distinction currently will have catastrophic consequences!
But Khor had already set off, and Noah felt what she felt through their brief connection during the memory viewing.
When it came to Hunger, the one quality he now understood intimately was this...whatever Hunger craved with sufficient potency, it would find.

Even if Khor didn't know precisely where Schrodinger was...though she did, because they'd been keeping tabs, with Schrodinger and Leonore currently hidden while observing a Justiciar complete its massacre in the Transcendent Quantum Folds with Noah's false illusions.
Even if she didn't know, her Hunger would track him and all his other bodies with inexorable certainty.
And she had already departed in her rage without questioning whether what they saw was truth, without wondering if they could actually face an existence with THE distinction at this moment.
Hunger was filled with fury!

chapters.title: Chapter 4400 You! II
paragraphs: Noah looked at Ozymandias, whose form had remained silent throughout the revelation.
His other self's body was changing, transforming more completely into The Way of Hunger, tentacles of obsidian-gold writhing with barely contained appetite.
He turned to Kael and the assembled Seed Members, his voice carrying command.
"Keep watch over things here. Maintain order. Do not let anyone leave the Isolated Civilization until I return."
He prepared to depart when Riya materialized beside him, her expression showing confusion mixed with determination.
"What the fuck is going on, Ancestor?" she demanded. "Whatever it is, I'm coming with!"
Noah didn't even reply.
Blue-gold Primus Mana erupted around both of them, wrapping their forms in concentrated authority as they vanished from the Isolated Civilization.
Behind them, Kael and the others stared in stupor at the titanic body of Ozymandias, which now dominated the sky with its impossible fusion of Mana and Hunger.
In the Transcendent Quantum Folds.
In a region covered by veils of silent Paradox, existence itself seemed uncertain...present and absent simultaneously, observable and unobservable in ways that made perception uncomfortable.
A Principle steeped in Paradox covered the entire region, making everything seem absolutely normal to observation while hiding profound abnormality beneath.
But within this veiled region, four beings resided.
Three were absolutely identical with only minor variations in their features...different aspects of the same existence manifested across compatible frameworks.
The fourth was Leonore Rureaux.
The three identical beings were all bodies of Schrodinger.
At this moment, two of them...a Living Concept Schrodinger and a Living Quantum Schrodinger, gazed outward toward distant regions beginning to fill with hazy white flames.
A Justiciar was decimating an entire Citadel of Living Quantums with systematic efficiency, its massacre proceeding exactly as expected.

The Living Paradox body of Schrodinger was with Leonore Rureaux in a more intimate configuration. They were embracing, veils of paradox covering their naked figures as Schrodinger stroked her hair with gentle affection.
Leonore tapped on his chest thoughtfully, her voice carrying concern.
"Should we really be doing this right now? Even if we cannot help it for the grander plan, Living Quantums are being killed..."
At such words, Schrodinger smiled and shook his head.

"No, they're actually not real Living Quantums. That Osmont is even more obscene than we initially assessed, he should be watching from nearby, but that entire domain is empty of life. Sophisticated illusions that took me considerable time to see through."
His smile widened.
"And hey, if we all might collapse soon in The Fallout, would you rather not have been doing this with me a few million more times?"
Leonore smiled at his logic, laying her head on his chest and feeling immense warmth radiating from his existence.
She nodded with contentment.
At such a time...
"YOU FUCKER!"
BOOM!
Existence above them split.
A terrifying aura descended with force that made the surrounding paradoxical veils shred like tissue paper.

Leonore and Schrodinger looked up in shock to see existence peeling around them like an onion, layers of reality being consumed by obsidian-crimson flames of Hunger that rapidly devoured the paradox protecting them.
They gazed upward to witness the visage of Khor descending.
They had seen her before around Osmont...small, diminutive, seemingly constrained. But not like this.

Now she looked down at them with a gaze so terrifying, so absolute in its murderous intent, that Schrodinger and Leonore understood immediately... this was the gaze of someone set on killing and collapsing, and such a gaze was directed exactly toward Schrodinger.
The moment he registered that callous, implacable stare, both he and Leonore felt terrifically oppressive power cascading down like a mountain about to crush them.
Not metaphorical pressure...existential weight that made their beings scream warnings of imminent termination.
Multiple Principles pulsed around the Paradox, Concept, and Quantum Schrodingers simultaneously as they mobilized defensive capabilities.
A collection of Quintillions in Complexity and Purity erupted around them!
Schrodinger's voice echoed out with desperate reasonableness.
"Whatever this is, there must be a mistake. Can we talk?"
An eruption of Principles and words, defensive authorities manifesting with speed that showed panic beneath calm exterior.
Yet against what descended from above, against an enraged Khor carrying dozens of Quintillions of Complexity and Purity alongside a fully realized Way of Existence refined through eons...
Khor gazed down with interminable rage.
She looked at Schrodinger.
And took a bite.
A single bite.
And in the next instant, Schrodinger's expression transformed from reasonable negotiation to shocked rage as his Living Quantum and Concept bodies stumbled backward paradoxically.
While his Living Paradox Body...
CRACK!
Split in half.

The entirety of that body's existence...its paradoxical nature, whether it was alive or dead, whether it could return from death and deny termination however many times through its fundamental frameworks...everything that represented it was consumed in a single bite.
The body that split in half was merely a husk, emptied of all essential nature, falling back into Leonore's horrified grasp.
One of Schrodinger's bodies, the most enigmatic and fantastical manifestation of the beggar known across existence, faced instant collapse as the wrath of The First Hunger descended without mercy.
Leonore Rureaux bellowed toward Khor with her own rage erupting, grief and fury mixing into something primal.
The two remaining bodies of Schrodinger gathered around her protectively, both seeming under immense strain from losing their third aspect so suddenly, so completely.
They gazed up at Khor.
Khor gazed back at them with eyes promising only continued violence.
And only at this moment...
From above, Noah and Riya materialized to witness the devastating scene.
One of Schrodinger's bodies collapsed, nothing but empty husk.
Khor floating above the survivors, gazing down coldly.
Her hands raised as her voice boomed across the region with authority that made existence itself tremble.
"You seem to enjoy plots. Machinations. Schemes within schemes within schemes."
Her crimson eyes blazed with accumulated rage of eons.
"It is good to see you again, O Existential Plotter... O Architect of Calculated Collapse... O Weaver of Predestined Catastrophes!"
The titles crashed down like judgments, each one carrying weight of accusation refined through endless suffering.

"I remember how you killed billions of Inevitabilities... slaughtered for your grand designs. I remember how you killed me, took my Heart, stole my Primacy, used everything I was as components for your precious Loom."
Her form blazed brighter, Hunger manifesting as physical force.

"From now on, I will collapse all remnants of you, THE Living Paradox. Every body. Every fragment. Every echo of your existence across all frameworks. You will know what it means to be devoured completely."
Her words crashed down with finality that suggested this was not threat but inevitable prophecy!

chapters.title: Chapter 4401 You! III
paragraphs: Noah stared at the terrifying scene of obsidian-crimson flames of Hunger bathing this entire region of the Transcendent Quantum Folds, painting existence in colors of annihilation rather than simple destruction.
His perception drank in the devastation all around...not just the immediate conflict, but the cascading consequences spreading outward.
In the distance, the Justiciar that had been conducting its systematic massacre had stopped.
Its hazy white form stood motionless, its featureless face turned toward their direction with what could only be interpreted as stupor...as if witnessing something that it absolutely did not expect.
Plans are falling apart.
The thought crossed Noah's mind.
They had intended to follow this Justiciar after its false genocide concluded, track it back to whatever base of operations these entities emerged from, gather critical information.
But now...
Noah shook his head, refocusing on the scene of devastation below where Khor already had her head raised, preparing to take another bite after exposing Schrodinger as THE Living Paradox.
We need to be certain.
He focused his gaze on The Living Concept Schrodinger and The Living Quantum Schrodinger, activating The Lens of Civilization with deliberate intent.
And prompts materialized above their heads.
|SUBJECT: Living Concept Schrodinger|
|SURFACE THOUGHT: Rage at loss of Living Paradox body - fragment of self terminated|
|DEEPER THOUGHT: Confusion at being called THE Living Paradox.|
|CORE EMOTION: A small sense of Fear at power the being above possesses - survival odds calculated as minimal|
|DEEPEST TRUTH: "THE Living Paradox? Me?! What the fuck is this bitch smoking?!"|
Noah's eyes shone sharply as he processed what The Lens revealed.
First, it showed this capability was truly terrifying!
Seeing inner truths, thoughts that beings themselves might not consciously acknowledge...
Oh!
And second...
Even Schrodinger himself does not believe he is THE Living Paradox.
But believing was one thing, and being was another entirely.

They had undoubtedly witnessed the image of Schrodinger, exactly as he appeared now, standing as THE Living Paradox over Khor's corpse in that recovered memory. The face was identical. The presence recognizable despite the shadowy obscuration.
So what's happening here?
Noah's eyes flashed sharply as he studied Schrodinger with renewed intensity, searching for answers to questions.
Is this something similar to Khor? Blocked memories or suppressed identity? Or is something else entirely going on—some manipulation or deception?
They needed to understand before rushing to collapse and destroy as he did not want to trigger anything catastrophic if things truly turned out to be the case.
Noah called out to Khor.

"Khor, lock them down if you must. Restrain, contain, prevent escape. But do not continue collapsing...not yet. Even these Schrodingers here do not believe in the depths of their existence that they are THE Living Paradox. Let us understand first. Hunger must be patient."
He understood her rage more intimately than she might realize.
Seeing inner truths, thoughts that beings themselves might not consciously acknowledge...

If someone had orchestrated his death, stolen his fundamental essence, killed his family, used his accumulated efforts as raw materials for their own designs....he might be doing exactly what she was attempting now.
But they needed understanding before committing to something irreversible.
Khor's figure trembled as she barely contained herself, her voice emerging strained as she kept her gaze locked onto the figures below.

"Outsider," she said, each word forced through clenched teeth, "I respect you a great deal even if I haven't expressed it directly. I am thankful for everything you have done for me, regardless of what I have contributed in return."
Her obsidian-crimson flames intensified.

"But this creature below me must die. Anything tied to THE Living Paradox must be collapsed...collapsed completely, whether it believes itself to be part of THE Living Paradox or not. I understand many things could be occurring. Remnant Will. Machinations. Deceptions. But what matters most is that it involves THE Living Paradox."
Her voice cracked slightly.

"Outsider, I understand your caution and appreciate your approach. But I must tell you there is not much time. The Paradoxical body I just collapsed...I intended to devour all of it. I hungered for every particle, every fragment of its existence. Yet I was only capable of splitting it in half and collapsing it completely."
She paused.

"For some reason, its corpse, its body was not capable of being devoured. Whatever may be occurring right now, Outsider, it is imperative that we do everything possible to turn every single iota of what is known as Schrodinger to less than ash. Before whatever is happening completes itself."
Her words caused Noah's eyes to pulse sharply as he looked down at the scene below.
Fucking hell.
His eyes flashed decisively.

The two remaining Schrodingers and Leonore Rureaux looked from Khor to Noah as if waiting for a voice of reason to calm things down, to negotiate, to find solutions through dialogue rather than violence.
But in the next moment, Noah gazed at them with coldness and immensity.
He sighed.
And...
BOOM!
His body erupted with radiant blue-gold Primus Mana, his entire existence seemingly becoming another heavy mountain about to crash down below without asking questions or seeking explanations.
At such a scene, the two remaining bodies of Schrodinger bellowed with shock and incredulity.

"WE ARE SCHRODINGER AND NOTHING ELSE!" they roared, their voices overlapping in desperate denial. "WE ARE A HERALD MEANT TO SAVE AS MUCH OF EXISTENCE AS POSSIBLE FROM THE COMING FALLOUT! WE ARE NOT THE FUCKING LIVING PARADOX!"
They screamed this while their Principles gathered around them!
But even as they protested, from above, Khor's mouth opened again to take another bite.
And Noah's existential weight came crushing down like an indomitable mountain accepting no resistance.
Schrodinger and Leonore Rureaux witnessed both forces descending simultaneously and howled with all their accumulated existence, power erupting in final desperate defense.
Yet the complexity of the bodies present...barely a few Quintillion combined, were too low compared to what they faced from above.
Decimation was the only possible outcome.
At such a terrifying moment in time, at such a critical juncture of existence...
"Wowee... that was unexpected. I've woken up a little early..."
HUUM!
A terrifically deep voice reverberated across all of nearby existence, resonating through dimensional frequencies.
Alongside it, all billowing forms of complexity and purity froze.
Above, Noah's gaze turned ashen as recognition crashed through his consciousness.
That voice.
He had heard it before...in Khor's recovered memory, speaking to THE Weavers with casual cruelty while holding her stolen Heart of Hunger.
The voice felt like corruption given sound. Deep and ancient, grating against existence itself as if its very presence was an offense to reality's established order.
Yet simultaneously, it commanded respect and reverence simply through being heard, as if acknowledging its presence was involuntary submission.
That...is the voice of THE Living Paradox.
Noah looked down as past Khor's livid figure, the two remaining Schrodingers paled.
They turned slowly, horror dawning across their features.
The corpse of the Paradoxical Schrodinger...which had been held by Leonore Rureaux, empty husk after Khor's devastating consumption, rose up with its two halves separated but moving.
A corpse by all reasonable definition. Terminated. Collapsed. Its existence ended.
And yet something utterly ancient billowed inside of it like smoke filling empty vessel.
The two halves of the corpse stretched, limbs extending in ways that defied the fact they were no longer connected.

Dark tendrils...not quite tentacles, not quite shadows, but something that existed in uncomfortable space between, erupted from the split edges and reached across the gap, seeking to rejoin severed halves.
The eyes of this corpse pulsed with sudden awareness, beginning to radiate pure crimson-gold light that suggested something vast occupying limited space.

And even before the halves fully reconnected, even while the body remained split down its center, the lips...also separated, moved independently yet in perfect synchronization, speaking with that deep, grating voice that made existence itself recoil.
"No... I could have sworn I collapsed you completely and took your Heart of Hunger..."
The corpse's head tilted with curiosity that bordered on mockery, crimson-gold eyes focusing on Khor above with recognition.
"How the heck are you still existing, Little Inevitability?"
All of Existence strained and shuddered.
As if a weight too heavy had appeared at a place it shouldn't.
Noah looked at it and understood one thing that would have been a potential reason for his failure in surviving The Fallout.
And the voice of this thing alone caused everything nearby to freeze.
Because this wasn't just power speaking.
This was THE speaking.
The voice of something that had reached scales of existence where normal rules became optional suggestions.
THE Living Paradox, in an unknown and unexpected capacity, had made an unimaginably early entrance!

chapters.title: Chapter 4402 You! IV
paragraphs: Existence itself changed.
The very fabric of reality became heavier, thicker, as if the surrounding space had transformed from air into viscous fluid that resisted all movement.
Breathing required conscious effort. Thought moved through molasses. Simply being demanded exertion that hadn't been necessary moments before.
DU! DU! DU!
From the surroundings, malevolent sounds began echoing, not from any specific source, but from everywhere, as if existence itself had become an instrument being played by unseen hands!
A grand orchestral symphony commenced, ushering the arrival of something that transcended classification.
DU!
The symphony felt like hymns echoing across dimensional frequencies, with existence itself manifesting words that pressed down with physical weight.
From all around, Noah felt an interminable level of pressure descend as it bellowed heavy proclamations.
REVERE! KNEEL! REVERE! KNEEL!
All of the surrounding existence seemed to have been commandeered, hijacked by will so vast it could treat reality as instrument for its declarations.
The terrifying pressure sank down from above and pressed upward from below, creating crushing vise that stated and demanded submission.
Noah felt such stifling pressure as his existence burned furiously in resistance, his expression heavy with the strain of refusing what reality itself was commanding.
Beside him, Riya was silently cursing with an angry expression, her voice forcing itself through clenched teeth.
"The only one I planned to get on my knees for is Little Ancestor!" she spat with defiant rage. "Fuck off!"
Oh!
The situation had turned heavy beyond anything they'd prepared for.
The situation had turned perilous in ways that made their previous challenges seem like preparatory exercises.

Noah focused on the horrific phenomenon below while resisting the symphony and hymns pressing down from all directions. He felt instinctively that the moment he submitted to these declarations...the moment he knelt as commanded, would be the moment he would be crushed completely, even before this entity turned its full attention toward him.
He was just emerging in his Way of Existence. He could not be extinguished now!
His Civilization was just starting. His people depend on paths he was forging!
He had to endure!

And so, as existence felt heavy and stifling and seeking to make him kneel with pressure exceeding even his own Cultivation Citadel's maximum settings, his being began radiating a terrific wave of blue-gold Primus Mana.
He called out with tyrannical certainty.
"Primus Singularity."
HUUM!
He invoked the ultimate capability of the Principle of Primus Ascension, designating his own existence as the focal point where Mana concentration and quality would reach theoretical maximums.
From far above, a brilliant blue-gold sun bloomed into existence...a singularity of concentrated power that made the surrounding Primus Mana seem diluted by comparison.
Its concentration grew and grew immensely, expanding while simultaneously compressing, creating paradoxical state where vastness and density existed together.

Noah felt himself bathed under the light of this Primus Singularity, and the sensation was profound...a sensation of fusion. He felt like he was one with it, his existence pulsing with grand distinction of his Way as...
The hymns and pressure stopped.
Not diminished. Not resisted. Simply ceased, as if the Primus Singularity's light had created space where those commands could not penetrate.
Noah observed Riya breathing easier, her expression showing relief mixed with awe as she looked at him and the brilliant sun above with shining eyes.
|PRIMUS SINGULARITY - ACTIVATION CONFIRMED|
|Duration: 1 hour at current complexity|
|Effect: All Mana-based operations functioning at 100x efficiency|
|Your advancement capabilities have been compressed into accelerated timeframes|
|Breakthroughs that would require decades will occur in minutes|
|Your existence is operating at theoretical maximum capability|
|WARNING: Extreme exertion detected across all systems|
|Perpetual Harvest is gathering accumulated effort with 100x multiplier|
|Cheating Architect is optimizing all processes for survival|
|CRITICAL OBSERVATION: You are facing an unsurpassable ordeal|
Unsurpassable.
The word blazed across Noah's consciousness with weight of absolute assessment.
But who decided that?!
BOOM!
His eyes blazed with tyranny even in this terrifically apocalyptic moment, refusing to accept predetermined outcomes regardless of how absolute they appeared.
Down below, the gaze of the Corpse of Schrodinger moved from Khor to land directly on Noah at this moment.
The separated halves of the corpse finished their horrific fusion, dark tendrils weaving flesh and essence back together in ways that defied natural healing.
The body became whole again...or at least, appeared whole, though something in its reconstituted form suggested it was merely wearing wholeness as temporary costume.
The moment Noah met that gaze...
BOOM!
His body vibrated as if struck by am invisible hammer.
The Primus Singularity above him trembled, its concentrated light flickering for the first time since manifestation.
A heavy sense of suffocation came from that gaze alone, as if being perceived by those crimson-gold eyes was physical assault against existence itself.
The Corpse of Schrodinger smiled...expression stretching too wide, carrying amusement that exceeded normal joy and approached something cruel.

"How interesting," the deep, grating voice emerged, each word making reality ripple with discomfort. "What a curious set of animals have gathered here. But why are you all so hasty? There is still time."
The smile widened impossibly further.
"Well, there was still time, and then you had to go and wake me... ah."
BOOM!

Each word landed with more weight than the last, and down below, Leonore Rureaux and the two remaining bodies of Schrodinger stood frozen in utter shock and horror...not at Khor, not at Noah, but at what was speaking through their reconstructed corpse.
Noah withstood the gaze while processing everything.
|You are bearing tremendous existential weight|
|Effort being exerted exceeds all previous recorded maximums|
|Perpetual Harvest is gathering this exertion with 100x efficiency|
|Even standing before this presence qualifies as monumental achievement|
|Your Primus Singularity is the only reason collapse has not yet occurred|
|Continue enduring - every moment survived generates advancement fuel|
Noah's existence pulsed as he forced himself to maintain eye contact with those crimson-gold eyes that seemed to smile at him before the voice continued.
"What a curious thing... is that a new Way of Existence that has bloomed in these glorious Folds? This is good... this is very, very good..."

Every time the voice echoed out, it made one feel like their existence was being dragged through spiked chains of concentrated weight, their very essence churning as if it would be turned inside out and examined from angles that shouldn't exist.
At such a moment, Khor's voice boomed out with effort.
Her body pulsed with utterly heavy crimson-obsidian light as she forced words through the oppressive atmosphere.
"Why... why did billions of Inevitabilities have to die? Why did you choose to do what you did?!"
At such words, the gaze of the Corpse of Schrodinger turned from Noah to focus on Khor exclusively.
Her body trembled with cold effort under that direct attention, and the Corpse smiled eerily as the heavy voice of THE Living Paradox boomed forth once more.
"Oh, you poor thing. You believe yourself to be a victim?"
The voice carried mockery mixed with something approaching pity.
It was not sympathy, but the condescending pity of vast intelligence observing limited understanding.

"Many billions collapsed, not just Inevitabilities. Nearly half of all Early Creatures turned to become The Dead. Multiple entities carrying THE distinction had their wings snapped off as they lost entire Civilizations they'd spent eons cultivating."
The crimson-gold eyes blazed brighter.

"And you believe yourself to be a victim? No, my dear Little Hunger. You were simply one consequence among countless others. You don't need a why. Existence doesn't need a why. Sometimes... things just happen, ya' know? Paradoxically. Gloriously. Without reason or purpose or grand design."
The voice took on lecturing quality, as if explaining obvious truth to child who should have learned better.

"There does not need to be justification for every action, motivation for every consequence. You were simply a cog in a very large weaving that needed adjustment. A component that required replacement for the machinery to continue functioning optimally."
The smile became even more terrible.

"Don't be filled with righteous rage and indignation. Don't take it personally, as if your suffering was about you. It wasn't. You mattered only insofar as your collapse served purposes beyond your comprehension. Sometimes, we would all be much happier just accepting things as they are and moving on rather than demanding explanations for every misfortune."
The voice dropped to something almost conversational, almost friendly.

"Look at where you are now. Somehow restored. Relevant again. Had you just accepted things and not collapsed this body in your rage, I wouldn't even be here right now, Little Hunger. Your insistence on vengeance for imagined injustices is what created this situation. You brought this upon yourself and everyone present through inability to simply... let go."
The devilish smile on the face of the Corpse of Schrodinger at those words was utterly terrifying.
But...it was not because it showed malice, but because it showed genuine amusement at philosophy it was expressing.
And right after finishing that monologue, it tapped out with one finger against empty air.
From all around, crimson-gold light bloomed with heavy presence that made the surrounding blue-gold of Noah's Primus Singularity seem fragile by comparison.
In front of Noah's eyes, a prompt materialized with urgency that suggested catastrophic development.
|WARNING: THE FESTIVAL OF PARADOX HAS BEEN CALLED FORTH|
|Classification: Unknown|
|Threat Level: Absolute|
|Survival Probability: Calculating...|
The Corpse of Schrodinger smiled brilliantly, expression carrying joy that exceeded sanity and approached something else in its terrible completeness.
Its voice emerged one final time before whatever came next:
"Sometimes, things just happen without reason or purpose. Cause becomes effect. Effect becomes cause. Everything and nothing occurs simultaneously."
The crimson-gold eyes blazed with light that made perception uncomfortable.
"Let me... show you."
BOOM!
Reality shattered.
And in the space where certainty had existed, paradox bloomed like flowers growing from burned ground, beautiful and terrible and absolutely inevitable.
The Festival had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 4403: Ormordnes I
paragraphs: Ormordnes.
The word carried heavy weight beyond its simple definition of despair.
Some across countless eras had attempted to capture its essence, to define what it meant when existence itself seemed to turn against hope.

Some held that Ormordnes wasthe recognition of unchangeable circumstance...the moment when one perceived that no amount of effort, no application of will, no intervention of fortune could alter what had already been set in motion.
It was not sadness at loss, but rather the profound acceptance that loss was inevitable and immutable.

To experienceOrmordneswas to understand that one’s struggle had always been futile, that the outcome was predetermined, and that all attempts to change it were merely theatrical gestures in a play whose ending had been written before its beginning.

Another perspective argued thatOrmordneswas...the weight of infinite responsibility meeting finite capability, the crushing realization that one was accountable for outcomes beyond one’s power to influence.
It emerged when duty exceeded capacity, when the role one occupied demanded more than existence could provide.
To feelOrmordneswas to understand simultaneously that onemustact and that onecannotsucceed, creating paradox that collapsed the will from within.
Both definitions carried truth. Both failed to capture the totality of what this word teuly meant!
At an unknown point in time, in the Earliest Folds where existence wore its most pristine and terrible forms, two beings sat together staring out onto an expanse of white.
THE CreatureandTHE Living Origin.
Two entities who carriedTHEdistinction, whose very presence made reality adjust its parameters to accommodate them.
They sat in silence for a time, two impossibilities sharing space and neither speaking, as if words themselves had become insufficient.
Eventually, THE Living Originspoke, and the voice that emerged seemed weary and tired.
"Do you know the word...Ormordnes?"
THE Creatureremained silent for a moment, its form utterly still as it contemplated the question.
Finally, it nodded.

"Ormordnes," THE Creature said, "is the state where one perceives clearly that all paths forward lead to unacceptable outcomes, yet remaining stationary is equally impossible. It is the recognition that existence has constructed circumstance where there areno correct choices...only varying degrees of catastrophe. To experienceOrmordnesis to understand that no matter what one does or does not do, collapse isinevitable."
The definition hung in the white expanse like a blaring accusation.
THE Living Originremained silent for a long moment after those words, as if processing their implications or perhaps confirming their accuracy through lived experience.

"I did not believe,"THE Living Originfinally said, voice breaking slightly, "that I could ever experience despair. After all, I amTHE Living Origin.Countless beginnings bloom from my weavings of existence."
The voice carried confusion mixed with profound disillusionment.
"How could Origin possibly experience despair? The very concept seems paradoxical...how can the source of beginnings encounter endings that cannot be transcended?"
Another pause, heavier than the first.
"And yet, on this day, at this moment... I feel that exact emotion with clarity that cannot be denied.I feel...Ormordnes. "
BOOM!
The words landed with existential weight, andTHE Creature’sperception expanded to truly observe their surroundings.
The scene was apocalyptic beyond normal comprehension.
Countless white-gold structures...grand architecture that had taken eons to construct, buildings that had served as foundational pillars for entire Civilization..lay shattered and cracked.
Some had been split cleanly as if by precision instruments. Others had simply...collapsed, their structural integrity unmade.
The entire region within the Folds was filled with ravenous Tears of Collapse...genuine rips in existence’s fabric.
Existence in the surroundings seemed to still be shuddering from whatever battle had occurred here, trembling like wounded creature that couldn’t comprehend the nature of its injuries.
THE Living Origin’sbody looked like blinding brilliance of light shining white-gold.
But at this moment, massive jagged tears permeated that brilliance...wounds that bled gold in slow, thick rivulets that stained the white expanse beneath.
The tears weren’t healing, weren’t closing, as if whatever had inflicted them had ensured they would remain open.
THE Living Origin’sgaze swept across the devastation of its Civilization, across the impossible scene of annihilation.
Trillions of unfathomably powerful Living Origins...beings whose Complexity had ranged in the Quintillions and even Sextillions, lay collapsed and dead.
Bodies that had contained enough power to reshape Folds now served only as monuments tocatastrophicfailure.

"You know,"THE Living Originsaid, voice carrying weight of shattered faith, "I always believed that whatever could possibly occur in the future, you would always be there for us. That as long asTHE Creature, this grand being who exceeded even otherTHEentities...was present, everything would ultimately be acceptable."
THE Creaturelistened to such words as its own existence felt tremendous strain, body shuddering lightly with effort.
THE Living Origincontinued, and the words emerged like confessions torn from unwilling source.
"But here we are, O Creature. My Civilization collapsed despite all our preparations and refinements. My very existence taken...claimed as if I were resource rather than sovereign power. And you..."
The voice broke completely.
"Just where did things go wrong? At what point did our path diverge from possibility of success? Why did you notsaveme, O Creature?"
Heavy silence bloomed at those words.
But...
Was it the job ofTHE Creatureto provide salvation? Why wouldTHE Living Originplace such expectation upon another being, even one carryingTHEdistinction?
The questions hung unanswered as eventually, THE Creaturelooked out into the distance...not at the devastation surrounding them, but at something beyond, something only it could perceive.
When it spoke, the words emerged with terrifying honesty.
"How could I succeed in saving others..."
"...when I could not succeed in saving myself?"
The confession landed like final nail in coffin of hope.
THE Creature...an entity that otherTHEentities looked toward for resolution...acknowledging its own inability to prevent catastrophe even for its own existence.
IfTHE Creatureitself was not immune, not capable of self-preservation against whatever forces had orchestrated this devastation...
What hope did anyone else possess?
Ormordnes.
Despair.

At certain points in existence, some beings experienced tremendous levels of such state and emotion. It did not necessarily mean that existence was against them or that reality had singled them out for persecution.
Maybe such beings were simply unlucky.
Maybe they were dealt bad hands through random distribution rather than targeted malice.
Maybe Existence operated without concern for fairness, and suffering was neither punishment nor lesson...merely consequence of being present when catastrophic events unfolded.
Who knew?

Certainly not those experiencingOrmordnes, who could only endure and wonder whether meaning existed in their collapse, or if they had simply been standing in the wrong place, at the wrong time...when inevitability descended!

Certainly not those experiencingOrmordnes, who could only endure and wonder whether meaning existed in their collapse, or if they had simply been standing in the wrong place, at the wrong time...when inevitability descended!

chapters.title: Chapter 4404 Ormordnes II
paragraphs: Noah did not like the feeling of not having control.

It was a simple truth for him...not about domination or absolute authority over others, but about maintaining sufficient influence over the immediate space around him, the moments that unfolded breath by breath.
He moved through existence with careful deliberation, ensuring that in the domains he touched, he held enough sway to react when circumstances shifted beneath his feet like sand in a tide.
Control meant that when conflict came, and it always came, he could at least oppose it. Could bear the weight!
Could dance along the edge of catastrophe without plummeting into its depths.
This was what he preferred: a measure of control, however small, regardless of what struggles pressed against him.
At this moment, he felt its absolute absence.
The air itself had changed.
It was thicker, heavier, as if existence had become viscous fluid that resisted all movement.
Breathing required conscious effort. Thought moved through something like honey. Simply being demanded exertion that moments ago had been effortless.
Around them, crimson-gold brilliance pervaded everything.
The light claimed, establishing dominion over space and time and the very possibility of action.
CRITICAL CATASTROPHE DETECTED
You have fallen into THE FESTIVAL OF PARADOX
The words materialized before Noah's vision with clinical precision, but he barely needed their confirmation.
He could feel the truth in his existence, in the way his Primus Mana guttered like flame in windstorm.
Due to vast disparity in the immensity of Civilizations between yours and THE Living Paradox's, all current weavings of expressed Civilizations have been suppressed completely.|
The Civilizational Chains of Paradox moved through the air like serpents of concentrated authority, and they had already wrapped around everyone present with discriminating precision.
Leonore Rureaux hung suspended, her considerable power rendered meaningless against constraints designed suppress entire
frameworks of existence rather than mere individuals.
The two remaining Living Schrodingers, Concept and Quantum, were similarly bound, their multiple natures collapsed into singular helplessness.
Khor floated immobilized, The First Hunger herself unable to devour despite that being the fundamental principle of her being.
And Noah, with Riya beside him, caught in the same terrible web.
The chains wrapped around limbs and stretched them in different directions, anchoring them in space so completely that even the smallest movement became impossible.
It was not merely physical restraint, this was existential binding!
The Quintillions of power they held within their beings meant nothing when the very Ways through which they expressed that power were shut down entirely.
Noah's Primus Singularity had dimmed to barely perceptible glow, a dying sun overwhelmed by foreign radiance. Only crimson-gold remained, absolute and inescapable.
The wind carried no scent of death, but something worse: the
absence of natural order, as if the rules governing how things should be had been temporarily suspended pending review by an authority that cared nothing for their restoration.
Noah looked at the chains binding him with the analytical focus that had me his nature.
Even now, even trapped and helpless, his mind worked with clarity.

The Lens of Civilization and his recent ascension into The Early Infinity Dominion Realm provided benefits that ran deeper than mere power...they granted understanding, a cool peace that crept over his thoughts even in the face of impossible odds.

The chains were actively suppressing his Primus Mana, preventing its expression through mechanisms that operated at civilizational scale. But as he observed them with enhanced perception, testing their constraints with the gentlest pressure of his will, he felt something interesting- they dimmed ever so slightly when his Way pressed against them.
Barely noticeable, like starlight competing with the sun, but real nonetheless.
Given time...seconds, minutes, perhaps longer, he could batter them endlessly. Even suppressed, the infinite nature of his reserves meant sustained assault remained possible.
He could potentially break free, though doing so would reveal abnormalities about his Way that he preferred to keep concealed. So I will observe. Collect information. Wait for the proper moment.

Panicking would accomplish nothing. Rage would change nothing. Screaming about wanting to live, about having people depending on him...such displays were luxuries for those who believed their emotions might influence outcomes.
Noah had learned better.
His gaze swept the tower of compressed authority they now
occupied, this space THE Living Paradox had claimed as absolutely as a king claims his throne.

To his right, Riya struggled furiously against her bonds. Her figure pulsed like a lamp fighting to stay lit, blue-gold Mana attempting to erupt from her body only to be snuffed the instant it manifested.
She had been looking at Noah the whole time, desperate to help despite her own helplessness.
When their eyes met, something in his steady gaze seemed to calm her. She stopped struggling, breathing heavily, finding composure in
his apparent lack of panic.
Noah turned his attention to the Corpse of Schrodinger standing before them. To THE Living Paradox inhabiting that reconstructed
flesh.
The entity closed its crimson-gold eyes and breathed in deeply, not from need, but as if savoring some quality of the air that others could
not perceive.
When it exhaled, the sound held satisfaction mixed with faint
distaste.

"The air itself smells nostalgic," THE Living Paradox said, voice making the surrounding space ripple like water struck by stone, "and yet dirtier than I remember. The air in THE Loom is much nicer...purified, refined, optimal for contemplation. Out here..."
The entity's expression twisted slightly. "Out here there are so many contaminants. Uncontrolled variables. Beings pursuing their own Ways without coordination or purpose beyond their limited
perspectives."
HUUM!
THE Living Paradox opened its eyes and gazed upon the bound
figures with expression mixing fondness and cruelty in equal measure. Its attention settled on Khor, and the smile that spread across the corpse's reconstructed face carried depths of meaning
Noah couldn't fully parse.
"Is this not simpler, Little Inevitability?" The voice was almost gentle, a teacher addressing a struggling student.
"Nobody throwing tantrums. Nobody raging about imagined injustices. This is how existence should be...moments of peace and clarity. Things happen, yes. Good and bad alike. But they do not have
to make us victims. We choose that designation through our refusal to
accept what
occurs."
As THE Living Paradox spoke, its figure floated through the crimson-gold light with serene grace, moving until it stood directly
before Khor.

Close enough that Noah could see the way Khor's eyes had changed...the livid rage draining away, replaced by the cold calculation of someone with eons of accumulated wisdom returning. Those who held years of philosophy were not immune to moments of weakness, to being blinded by emotion. But if they could control themselves, return to paths of discipline...
Khor had a momentary lapse. That was all.
THE Living Paradox examined Khor with clinical interest, gaze
traveling up and down her bound form like an artist assessing a
canvas.

"How wondrous," it said, "It truly is you, not fragment or echo, but actual restored existence. Though infinitely weaker. Even though you faced complete collapse of your very Way. Even though I personally
unmade you and claimed your Heart of Hunger..." The crimson-gold eyes blazed brighter. "You stand before me again. Impossible, and yet here you are. How did you accomplish this?"

chapters.title: Chapter 4405 Ormordnes III
paragraphs: The entity tilted its head, serpentine and strange.

"All the Inevitabilities should be bound to THE Loom, you understand. The entirety of their existence in constant state of agony and pain as their being is continuously drained while they seek endlessly for more. Their Hunger growing without possibility of satisfaction, a perfect perpetual motion engine of suffering and power generation." The words were spoken with the same tone one might use to describe mundane things- factual, detached, utterly unconcerned with the horror they described.
Khor's eyes flashed sharply, but she refused the bait. She closed her eyes briefly, wondering about the truthfulness of those claims, whether her people truly suffered in such endless torment.
The silence seemed to delight THE Living Paradox further.
"Come now," it said, voice taking on coaxing quality.

"I am genuinely curious. Very few could reverse collapse...especially collapse executed by me personally. Did THE Creature somehow manage this? But that entity shouldn't be able to act freely anymore, not after what I arranged..."
It paused, considering.
"Was it THE Living Temporal? Did that little rat perform temporal manipulation? That would be characteristic, though I thought we'd accounted for such interference..."
Questions poured forth, but Khor remained silent, ancient discipline holding firm at this momemt.
THE Living Paradox's smile became eerily serene, and in that moment Noah felt the temperature of danger shift from warm threat to cold certainty.
"Well," the entity said softly, "if you won't tell me, I'll simply dig
through your existence itself. Examine your fundamental
architecture. Trace the mechanisms of your restoration. Identify the culprit responsible..."
Schrodinger's hand reached out toward Khor with calm confidence, fingers extending!
And in that instant, Khor's crimson eyes blazed as something settled over her consciousness like a shroud.
Noah recognized it immediately, though he'd never felt its weight himself.
Ormordnes.
Despair...not for her own destruction, but for what her examination might reveal about him.
Through whatever connection they'd forged, her voice touched his mind.
"I... am sorry, Outsider."
The words carried finality that made Noah's existence run cold. Not apology for failure. Not regret for circumstances.
Goodbye.
She...planned to collapse herself before examination could occur. To unmake her own existence rather than risk revealing his involvement in her restoration. To Hunger...and Hunger completely.

Noah's eyes shifted, and light of obsidian-crimson leaked from them like blood from a wound...something deeper than his blue-gold Primus Mana, primal and hungry and utterly unbound by the Festival's constraints, and yet still pulsing as if it were the same Way of Existence.
The prompts had been specific...all current weavings of expressed Civilizations have been suppressed.
All current. All expressed.
When the Festival descended, he had been expressing only his Way of Mana.
His other Way...newer, rawer, less refined, had been dormant.
Unexpressed.
And therefore, unbound.
"Arise," Noah said quietly, calling to his Hunger.
BOOM!
Obsidian-crimson brilliance erupted from him like thousand hungry mouths opening simultaneously, jaws of infinite appetite manifesting in the space around him.
He felt his existence extend through them, consciousness distributed across devouring force that recognized no limitation save its own
appetite.
The countless jaws snapped onto the Civilizational Chains of Paradox.
CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!
The sound drew THE Living Paradox's gaze instantly, those
crimson-gold eyes widening with surprise.
For a heartbeat, Noah was far in the distance, bound and helpless.
In the next heartbeat...
POP!
He stood directly behind Khor, immediately before THE Living Paradox, as obsidian-crimson waves of Hunger spread outward like smoke given terrible purpose, devouring chains of Paradox with
methodical hunger.
Noah wrapped his arms around Khor and pulled her back from the reaching hand, and THE Living Paradox simply watched, apparently amazed that escape was even possible within its absolute domain.
Even knowing this situation remained impossible, even understanding they could not match the entity before them, Noah moved with calm born of discipline rather than hope.
He danced along the edge of tumultuous waves, waiting to see how he would emerge on the other side...if he emerged at all.
As he retreated with Khor in his grasp, he activated The Lens of Civilization, focusing on THE Living Paradox with every enhancement his ascension had granted.
He wanted to see weaknesses, understand mechanisms, identify any
advantage...
And saw nothing.
Target's complexity far exceeds your own existence]
No possible weavings obtained
The words were clear as carved stone, absolute as death.
Noah's expression grew heavier, but he whispered to Khor as his Hunger continued its feast.
"Don't try to do that again, even if things seem impossible!" His voice carried that commanding tone it had adopted since he
began walking Two Ways, since he'd stepped into The Early Infinity Dominion Realm.
Not louder, but heavier, as if the words themselves carried existential
weight.
Khor's ancient eyes studied him, then she sighed and nodded lightly.
"Okay, Outsider. But it seems I have drawn you into a point of no
return."
Noah arrived beside Riya again, his obsidian-crimson Hunger continuing its meal of paradoxical chains.
The consumed material flowed into some internal repository...he would examine it later, if there was a later.
For now, every scrap of attention needed to remain focused on the
entity before them.
Because even after accomplishing this minor impossibility, he still felt that prickling sensation of vastly superior power pressing down from
all sides.
THE Living Paradox's full attention had turned upon him.
"Now," the entity said, voice carrying delighted interest, "you have
garnered my complete attention. You are very weak...barely worth noticing by normal standards, yet somehow you violated the rules of my Festival. The constraints should be absolute for beings at your
level." The corpse's head tilted as if accessing memories from the flesh it inhabited.
Recognition sparked in those crimson-gold eyes soon after.
"Ah! The Early Creature, Osmont, yes? And you have begun spreading
your Way like a small child who just discovered fire and wants to show everyone what bright things it can make..." THE Living Paradox's
smile widened. "My oh my, how cute."
The words mixed condescension with genuine amusement, as if
observing precocious infant attempting tasks far beyond its capability. Noah continued staring at the entity while his mind raced through
possibilities of survival, each one examined and discarded as insufficient.
His Complexity, his Principles, his carefully cultivated capabilities....all seemed woefully inadequate against power operating at this scale. Then, a thought crystallized with desperate clarity.
If I lack the power to resolve this... could I call someone who
possesses such power?
Someone like...Anaximander?
HUUM!
Existence howled around them, carrying neither hope nor despair but
simply the weight of moment stretched thin, ready to snap in whichever direction fate decreed.
And THE Living Paradox continued watching with that terrible,
amused smile, waiting to see what the small child playing with fire would attempt next.
